# Intake Brief — Ship skill: Discord release notification

**Work item:** SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z — Ship skill: send Discord message with release details + changelog on successful release (`feature`, priority `medium`)

## Problem statement

When the ship skill completes a successful release (dev → main), there is currently no automatic notification; operators must poll GitHub/worklog to learn what shipped. We want the ship skill to post release details — including the changelog — to a Discord channel on every successful release.

## Users

- **Operator / release manager (human)** — wants a record of each release in a Discord channel without manually checking GitHub.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when a release ships successfully, I want a Discord message with the version, tag, PR link, and changelog posted to a channel I configure, so my team sees what shipped without checking GitHub."
- **Team members watching the Discord channel** — consume the release summary passively.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After a **successful, non-dry-run** release (verified landed on `origin/main`), the ship skill posts a Discord message to the configured channel containing: released version, git tag (`vX.Y.Z`), release date, PR URL, and the new version's changelog section from `CHANGELOG.md`.
- AC2 — Config resolution: the per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` `discord.webhook_url` takes precedence over the global fallback (`~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`, same key). If neither is set, no message is sent and the release completes normally (logged, not an error).
- AC3 — Notification is **non-blocking**: a failed or slow webhook POST logs a warning and does not change the release exit code; a release that already landed is never failed by a notification failure.
- AC4 — The webhook payload respects Discord limits (embed description ≤ 4096 chars); an over-long changelog is truncated with an ellipsis marker.
- AC5 — Unit tests cover: config precedence + skip-when-unset, changelog extraction/truncation, payload shape, and non-blocking failure behavior. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (ship skill `SKILL.md` and its reference docs, including config schema and behavior).

## Constraints

- Code lives in the **global agent skill** `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/` (not the repo); per-project config lives in the repo's `.worklog/config.yaml`.
- No new runtime dependencies: Node.js 18+ is already a prerequisite; use the built-in `fetch` for the webhook POST.
- The webhook URL is a **secret** (contains an auth token) — must not be committed to the repo; the global fallback file lives outside the repo. Config schema must be documented as sensitive.
- Must not alter existing gating, exit codes, or the Code Freeze contract.
- Notification is a post-release concern — it must run only after release-merge verification (never on `--dry-run` or failed releases).

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` orchestrates the release: 5 gates → `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (bump version, generate `CHANGELOG.md`, merge, tag `vX.Y.Z`, push, PR) → wait PR merge → `syncDevWithMain()` → `verifyReleaseMerge(version)` → `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)`.
- `generate-changelog.js` writes `CHANGELOG.md` at repo root with sections `## vX.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` and Features / Bug Fixes / Other categories.
- Ship currently reads **no** config file; the per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` (projectName, prefix, autoExport, autoSync) is the established config convention.
- No existing Discord/webhook integration in the agent infra or this repo; no `DISCORD_*` env vars set.

## Desired change

Add a new post-release step in `run-release.js` (after `verifyReleaseMerge()` succeeds, alongside the close-work-items step) that:

1. Resolves the webhook URL: per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` → `discord.webhook_url`, falling back to global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` → `discord.webhook_url`. Unset → log info, skip, proceed.
2. Extracts the new version's changelog section from `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Builds a Discord embed payload (version, tag, date, PR URL, changelog description truncated to ≤ 4096 chars).
4. POSTs to the webhook via built-in `fetch`; on any failure logs a warning and returns non-blocking (release exit code unchanged).
5. Dry-run / failed releases never trigger a notification.

New module `discord-notify.js` (config resolution, changelog extraction, payload build, send) with injectable fetch for tests; new unit tests under the skill.

## Key Files:

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — add Step 8.5: call `sendReleaseNotification()` after merge verification succeeds (non-blocking).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — **new**: webhook URL resolution (project → global), changelog section extraction + truncation, embed payload builder, non-blocking `fetch` POST.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/SKILL.md` — document the notification behavior, config schema (`discord.webhook_url`), and non-blocking semantics.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — update reference docs (schema, hook point).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/tests/test_discord-notify.js` — **new**: unit tests (config precedence, skip-when-unset, truncation, payload shape, non-blocking failure).
- `.worklog/config.yaml` (per-project) / `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (global) — config schema consumed (webhook URL is secret — document gitignore/redaction).

## Related work

- `LP-0MSQ0NTMO00577UJ` — "ship skill getCandidateItems(): 'set -o pipefail' fails on dash..." (prior ship-skill maintenance; same skill, adjacent scripts).
- `LP-0MSQ0NI7K009UDE8` — "Release v0.1.13 (dev → main)" (example ship usage/evidence of release flow).
- No existing work item covers release notification or Discord integration (searched: discord, release notification, ship skill).
- Automated find-related report (inserted into item description by the skill) surfaced three low-relevance keyword matches: `LP-0MN8LU516006M2SN` (Co-residency runtime support), `LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H` (Qwen3 reasoning_content fix), `LP-0MRCU7PTG005VVD4` (Content-Encoding gzip header) — matched on generic words (config/channel/release/skill); none are actionable related work.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — secret leakage:** webhook URL committed to a repo. *Mitigation:* document as sensitive; prefer the global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (outside repos); AC2 covers precedence so a repo can override but needn't store the secret.
- **Risk — notification latency/flakiness:** network hiccup hangs the release. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout on the POST; non-blocking warning on failure (AC3).
- **Risk — Discord rate limits / message size:** >4096-char changelog or 429 responses. *Mitigation:* truncation (AC4); treat 429/5xx as a logged warning (AC3).
- **Assumption — message content:** version, tag, date, PR URL, and changelog section are the "details of the release" requested; no changelog section found → send without changelog (or skip changelog field) rather than fail.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra ideas (e.g., notify on *failed* releases, Slack/email adapters, rich per-item links) are recorded as separate work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "Where should the Discord channel be configured? (a) per-project `.worklog/config.yaml`; (b) global config `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`; (c) both — global default + per-project override?"
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(c)" — per-project with a global fallback. Final accepted answer: per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` `discord.webhook_url` with global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` fallback. Prior answers: none changed. Research: ship skill reads no config today; `.worklog/config.yaml` is the established per-project convention (projectName/prefix); `~/.pi/agent/` is the global agent-config home (auth.json, models.json, settings.json) — no existing global YAML config, so `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` is a new, natural location.
- **Q2:** "What Discord integration mechanism? (a) Webhook URL in config; (b) bot token + channel ID."
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(a)" — webhook URL. Final accepted answer: webhook URL (a webhook is bound to one channel; no bot/channel-ID plumbing needed). Research: no prior Discord integration exists in the repo or agent infra (grep: webhook/discord → only LLM session recordings and node_modules READMEs).
- **Q3:** "If the Discord message fails to send, should the release (a) still succeed — log a warning (non-blocking); (b) be treated as a release failure (blocking)?"
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(a)" — non-blocking warning. Final accepted answer: notification failure never fails an already-landed release; warn and continue. Research: release flow already treats post-merge steps non-blockingly (close-work-items step is non-blocking); consistent with that precedent.

# Local Skill Extensions for Global Skills

**Headline:** Define and implement a convention (`.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/`) that lets an invoking project augment any global skill with project-local prose hooks and a machine-readable data file, without forking or editing the global skill.

## Problem

Global skills (intake, plan, implement, audit, test, …) shipped by this
repository are static. A project that needs project-specific behaviour inside a
global skill today must either fork the skill or hardcode project specifics in
the global copy — neither is acceptable. There is no discovery convention, no
loader, and no machine-readable extension point, so per-project test
strategies, gates, and data maps cannot be supplied from the consuming repo.

## Users

- **Project maintainer** — wants to add project-specific behaviour (e.g. typed
  test profiles, extra validation) to a global skill from their own repo,
  without editing `~/.pi/agent/skills` or this repository.
- **Implementing/release agent** — runs a global skill from a project cwd and
  expects any local extension to be discovered and applied automatically.
- **Consumer work item** (SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6 — Test skill `--type`) — requires
  a *machine-readable* type→command map under this convention so the test
  runner can delegate without parsing prose.

Example user stories:

- *As a project maintainer,* I add `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`
  with my `unit`/`smoke` commands and `/skill:test --type unit` uses them — no
  global-skill change.
- *As an agent,* running a global skill in a project with
  `.pi/skills_extensions/<skill>/SKILL_PREFIX.md` applies that project guidance
  before the skill's first actionable step.
- *As a maintainer,* a project without any extension directory sees byte-for-byte
  unchanged behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Convention and discovery.** A global skill resolves its project extension
   from `<project_root>/.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/`, where
   `<project_root>` is the invoking project's git root (falling back to cwd
   when not in a git repo). Discovery is repo-root-scoped and documented; it
   must not invent a second discovery path alongside `.pi/test-config.json`.
2. **Prose hooks.** Optional `SKILL_PREFIX.md` and `SKILL_POSTFIX.md` in that
   directory are surfaced to the agent (prefix before the skill's first
   actionable step, postfix after its final step) and are strictly additive to
   the global skill.
3. **Machine-readable extension.** An optional JSON file
   (`extension.json`) in the same directory is parsed by a shared loader and
   exposed to skill scripts; a malformed file or invalid shape produces a
   clear diagnostic naming the file — never a silent fallback. A work item
   consuming the mechanism (SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6) must be able to resolve a
   machine-readable type→command map through it.
4. **Precedence and safety.** Absence of the directory is a no-op (no error,
   no behaviour change). Extensions augment global behaviour and must not be
   able to disable or weaken a skill's safety/gating steps (plan approval,
   audit gates, build→test→commit order).
5. **Loader tests.** `skill/shared/skill_extensions.py` is covered by unit
   tests: present/absent directory, prefix-only / postfix-only, valid and
   malformed JSON, unknown extra keys, and project-root resolution from a
   nested cwd; at least one end-to-end consumer demonstration is included.
6. **Documentation.** The convention is documented in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and a
   maintainer reference (`docs/dev/skill-extensions.md`), cross-referenced
   from `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, with schema guidance, precedence,
   trust/security notes, and an explicit statement that global skill
   behaviour is unchanged when no extension exists. UK English throughout.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Uk English in all docs, help text, and comments.
- Must not hardcode project-specific behaviour (e.g. Tableau Card Engine
  test profiles) into the global skill.
- Must not conflict with pi-native project skills (`.pi/skills/`): extensions
  are additive fragments, not replacement skill definitions.
- Must work from any cwd, including a git worktree and when a skill is invoked
  with `--worklog-dir`; project-root resolution must be robust.
- Keep it small: two optional prose files plus one optional JSON file per
  skill — no plugin system, no schema DSL.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` has a compactness budget (SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP, ≤8 KB up
  from a smaller baseline); the added convention text must be concise and may
  link out to the maintainer reference.

## Existing state

- **No convention exists on disk.** A repo-wide grep for `skills_extensions`,
  `SKILL_PREFIX`, and `SKILL_POSTFIX` across `*.py`/`*.md`/`*.mjs`/`*.json`
  returns zero matches (excluding worktrees/caches).
- **Global skills are installed by symlink** — `scripts/install_pi.sh` links
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/` tree; skills reference scripts via
  `$(skill_path <name>)`.
- **Pi-native project skills are a separate mechanism** — pi loads project
  skills from `.pi/skills/` (and `.agents/skills/`) after the project is
  trusted (pi `docs/skills.md`, "Locations"). They *replace/compete* with
  global skills of the same name; they are not additive fragments.
- **Machine-readable per-project extension precedent already exists** —
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` reads `<root>/.pi/test-config.json`
  (`suiteCommands`, `timeoutPerCommand`), proving the project-root JSON pattern
  works from any cwd via `detect_project_root()`.
- **Blocking consumer:** SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6 (child, priority critical) cannot
  be implemented until this convention (and its machine-readable file) lands.
- **Stale description text:** the seed's "Pi Ecosystem Research Findings: See
  analysis below for alternatives considered." has no following analysis —
  recorded as an open question.

## Desired change

1. Define the convention: `.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/` containing
   optional `SKILL_PREFIX.md`, `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`, and `extension.json`.
2. Implement `skill/shared/skill_extensions.py`: resolve the invoking project
   root, load the three optional files, expose them as a typed result, and
   emit clear diagnostics for malformed data.
3. Document it in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (agent-facing, concise) and
   `docs/dev/skill-extensions.md` (maintainer reference); cross-reference
   `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`.
4. Wire the hook into the global skill flow (the agent reads prefix/postfix
   for the active skill; scripts call the loader) and prove the mechanism with
   the test-skill consumer (SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6).
5. Add tests for the loader and a fixture-based end-to-end demonstration.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/skill_extensions.py` — new: project-root resolution, extension discovery, JSON parsing, diagnostics, precedence rules.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_skill_extensions.py` — new: unit tests for present/absent/partial/malformed cases and nested-cwd root resolution.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — document the convention and the agent instruction to load prefix/postfix for the active skill (concise; links to the reference).
- `docs/dev/skill-extensions.md` — new: maintainer reference (contract, schema guidance, precedence, trust/security, examples).
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — cross-reference the extension convention alongside the existing path-resolution rules.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — consumer-facing pointer showing how a skill consumes the machine-readable map (implemented with SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — reference consumer of the machine-readable map (implemented with SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (to confirm):** the convention path is `.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/` and the machine-readable file is `extension.json`. *Mitigation:* keep the loader path/filename constants in one place so a rename is a one-line change.
- **Assumption (to confirm):** discovery is repo-root-scoped (git root, cwd fallback), not ancestor-walking like pi project skills. *Mitigation:* document explicitly.
- **Risk (external):** pi may add native per-project skill extension support, superseding this convention. *Mitigation:* keep the loader thin, document the convention as project-local and replaceable, and record an Open Question.
- **Risk (security/trust):** extension fragments are arbitrary instructions/commands from the project. *Mitigation:* document that extensions carry the same trust as project skills and cannot bypass safety gates (AC4).
- **Risk (surface):** pointing every `SKILL.md` at the convention touches ~20 files. *Mitigation:* document once in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, add per-skill pointers only where a skill actually consumes extensions; scripts use the shared loader directly.
- **Risk (context budget):** added guidance inflates the always-loaded `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`. *Mitigation:* concise wording + link to the reference (SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP).
- **Risk (scope creep):** pressure to build a plugin/DSL system. *Mitigation:* fixed scope — two prose files + one JSON file; further ideas become separate work items.

## Related work

- **SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6** — Test skill `--type` parameter (child, blocking consumer; requires the machine-readable map).
- **SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W** — Split global vs project AGENTS.md (completed) — same global/project boundary rationale.
- **SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR** — Reduce initial LLM context from skills (completed) — extension prose must not bloat startup context.
- **SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP** — Compact AGENTS_GLOBAL.md to ≤8 KB (completed) — budget constraint on the added guidance.
- **SA-0MSNQV9J20010LE7** — Test skill project-root resolution (`detect_project_root`) — precedent the loader should mirror (open; implementation present in `run_tests.py`).
- **SA-0MSAC1IAS007I3K8** — Wire test skill into code-touching skills and master AGENTS (completed) — related wiring work, not blocking.
- pi documentation: `docs/skills.md` (skill locations, project skills, progressive disclosure) — consulted for the native-mechanism comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was held: the operator issued a direct "continue" and
the seed context (problem/goal/proposed approach) plus the blocking child's
hard constraints were sufficient to draft the brief. The design points below
were resolved with **documented assumptions** that require producer
confirmation; each is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION rather than silently
decided.

- **Q: Where do extensions live, and is discovery repo-root or ancestor-walking?** — **OPEN QUESTION (assumed).** Assumption: `<project_root>/.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/`, resolved via git root with cwd fallback (mirroring `detect_project_root()` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`). Rationale: matches the existing `.pi/test-config.json` precedent and avoids the ambiguity of ancestor walking. Evidence: repo grep for `skills_extensions` returns no matches; `detect_project_root()` uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- **Q: What is the machine-readable format/filename?** — **OPEN QUESTION (assumed).** Assumption: `extension.json` (parsed JSON, schema owned by each skill). The blocking child (SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6) specifies the test skill's `types` schema and may also read `.pi/test-config.json`; the parent's job is to define discovery + the generic container, not the test schema. Rationale: the child's constraint requires a machine-readable file "inside the same `.pi/skills_extensions/test/` directory".
- **Q: Do extensions augment or replace global skills?** — **ANSWER (derived from the brief's "Proposed Approach"):** augment. The seed explicitly says prefix "executed after gating steps, before the first actionable step" and postfix "after the final step completes" — additive hooks around the unchanged global workflow. Recorded as AC4 (extensions must not weaken safety gates).
- **Q: How does this interact with pi-native project skills (`.pi/skills/`)?** — **ANSWER (research).** Pi loads project skills from `.pi/skills/`/`.agents/skills/` after trust; same-name project skills warn and the first found wins (pi `docs/skills.md`). They are *whole-skill replacements*, not additive fragments, so this convention is complementary and must not be conflated with them (recorded as a constraint).
- **Q: What happened to the "Pi Ecosystem Research Findings" referenced in the description?** — **OPEN QUESTION.** The seed says "See analysis below for alternatives considered" but no analysis follows. This brief supplies the missing pi-ecosystem comparison (native project skills vs additive fragments); the producer may restore or discard the original research text.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKZN9S8000V94N** – Document wl search strategies in AGENTS_GLOBAL.md: never use bare wl list, document wl list <term> vs wl search (completed)
- **SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH** – Remove skill/ralph/ directory tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSMBD3XV002AEMB** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py:22 — Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `E402`) (RUF100) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: actionable, allowing, allows, analysis, approach (+44 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: allows, analysis, audit, augment, based (+33 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: actionable, alternatives, analysis, audit, based (+31 more)

## Goal

Reduce wasted re-audit work in the release pipeline: audits that are redundant (item already audited at the same HEAD) or stale (code changed after the audit) currently trigger full re-runs — each costing 15-45 min of model time. Make re-audits the exception, not the norm.

## Background (observed during 2026-08-12 release of SorraAgents)

1. **Redundant audit by a second session**: Map re-audited SA-0MSOK041Z0027964 (already completed + audited by another session at the same HEAD, verdict Ready to close: Yes, ~19:00). ~1 hour of model time spent repeating a passed audit. Root cause: no coordination check (`wl audit-show` / status / comments) before launching a re-audit, and no fast-path that short-circuits when a fresh audit already exists.
2. **Stale audits after post-audit commits**: the 9 children of SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ were audited, then 2 more commits landed on dev (49a32769 test-fix, e7266ccc AC1 scoping) touching the same files — every one of the 9 audits went stale and had to be re-run (~2.5 h of audits). Root cause: audit freshness is keyed on the audited file content, but the fingerprint did not incorporate the commit/HEAD at audit time; SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ (working-tree state in fingerprint, completed) is the first step but does not yet key freshness on commit hash.
3. **Transient/timeout re-runs**: SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP and the parent SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ audit-1 both timed out under model contention and were re-run once the slot freed — unavoidable, but a queue/slot-stagger hint would reduce the retry rate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` records the git commit hash (HEAD) at audit time in the persisted audit record; freshness check considers an audit stale if HEAD moved since the audit ran (in addition to content fingerprint).
2. Before starting a full audit, the runner (or the audit skill docs) surfaces an existing fresh audit: `wl audit-show <id>` shows "Ready to close: Yes" with auditedAt >= last commit touching audited files → the runner prints a fast-path notice and exits (or prompts) instead of re-running the model.
3. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and the audit skill reference docs document the coordination check: always run `wl audit-show <id>` + `wl comment list <id>` first; do not re-audit an item that is completed/in_review with a fresh audit unless the code changed.
4. Measurable: re-audit count in one release cycle drops (target: 0 redundant re-audits — only stale/forced re-audits allowed); verified by a test that audits twice at the same HEAD and asserts the second run short-circuits without invoking the model.

## Out of scope

- Changing audit verdict semantics or the audit gate itself.
- Fixing model-contention timeouts (separate concern, tracked elsewhere).
- The two currently-open critical items blocking release (SA-0MSQ72BVV0011SRU, SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T).

Related: SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ (working-tree fingerprint — first step, completed); discovered during release work on SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ.

# Problem statement

When the implement skill encounters a work item that has already been implemented (e.g. the skill detects a commit where the work was completed but the item is in a wrong state/stage, or an audit identifies gaps in what was done), it should review the most recent audit report, fix any identified gaps inline, and proceed — rather than blindly re-implementing or silently skipping.

## Users

- **Agent executing `/skill:implement <id>`**: needs to handle the "already completed" case deterministically without manual intervention or blind re-implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detect "already implemented"** — the implement skill recognizes when the work has already been completed (e.g. via commit history, status/stage mismatch, or an audit report indicating prior completion).
2. **Review audit report** — when already implemented is detected, fetch/review the most recent audit report for the item (`/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
3. **Close gaps inline** — if the audit reveals gaps (unmet ACs, failing tests, missed requirements), fix them inline as part of the current item's implementation (option b per intake clarification, 2026-08-13) — NOT by creating new work items.
4. **Skip if clean** — if the audit shows no gaps, report the summary and skip further implementation (no re-work).
5. **Update documentation** — the implement skill's `SKILL.md` is updated to describe this new step and its logic.

## Constraints

- Changes are scoped to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and corresponding doc hygiene tests.
- No new work items should be created for gaps — they are closed inline.
- Follow the existing implement skill structure (add a numbered step, consistent formatting).

## Existing state

The implement skill has no logic to detect when a work item has already been implemented. It proceeds through all steps regardless, which can lead to redundant work or missed gap remediation when an item's state/stage is out of sync with its actual implementation status.

## Desired change

Add a new step in the implement skill (between Step 3.1 "Definition gate" and Step 4 "Create a worktree") that:
1. Checks whether the item has already been implemented
2. If yes: reviews the latest audit report, identifies gaps, and fixes them inline
3. If no: proceeds to the normal workflow

## Risks & assumptions

- **Detection signal ambiguity** — "already implemented" must be driven by the implement skill's own output (it reports completion with a commit hash), not inferred from status alone; document the exact detection trigger in the skill.
- **Audit staleness** — the most recent audit report may predate later fixes; reuse a fresh audit (same guidance as existing Step 3: reuse a recent audit, else `/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
- **Scope creep in inline gap-closing** — large gaps discovered via audit are potential new work items; keep inline fixes minimal and record extra opportunities as linked work items (discovered-from), not scope.
- **Dependency on audit output format** — logic reads the audit report; keep the reading step aligned with how the audit skill persists reports (`audit_report_<id>.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add the new step with detection logic and audit review procedure
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — Ensure doc hygiene tests still pass

## Related work

- SA-0MSAS108O009DYKT — audit skill must write audit report files with unique names
- SA-0MPGU5QG40040AWS — Move recent-audit bootstrap into implement skill
- SA-0MPMGES67002AP0Z — Implement per-child audit loop in Ralph

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as 'already implemented'?" — Answer (operator): option d — the implement skill itself sometimes reports the work is already completed and points to a commit hash; in that situation the item is either (a) completed but in the wrong state/stage, or (b) a problem with the implementation was identified in an audit. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.
- Q2: "What does 'close them' (the gaps) mean?" — Answer (operator): option b — fix the gaps inline as part of the current item's implementation, then proceed to in_review. No new work items for gaps. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.

## Summary

Follow-up to SA-0MSLLGDW00098UCC (audit_runner git resolution cwd-dependence), deliberately scoped OUT of that item.

Once git-derived content (file-scope manifest, changed-file list, HEAD sha, working-tree hash) follows the worklog-derived owning project root, the remaining launch-cwd-bound consumers are:

- `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` itself (`_detect_project_root`, audit_runner.py:681) — resolved at import time from the launch cwd.
- Code-quality scan `project_root` (:1536, :1629, :1708).
- Debug-log path (:3645).
- `_repo_index` fallback directory listing (:3007).

## Goal

Make `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` per-audit dynamic (resolved from the worklog store / item prefix like the git pieces), so the documented pattern 'launch the runner from the skill install directory (or any other cwd) and audit items in a different project's worklog' holds end-to-end.

## Design considerations

- Inverts the launch-context guard policy (LP-0MSQ32HNR007AI6B): a launch from a non-owning cwd with a correct `--worklog-dir` becomes legitimate instead of aborting; the guard's fail-fast role shrinks to the undeterminable-ownership case.
- Existing guard tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py) assert abort-on-mismatch and must be inverted/extended.
- Worktree audits (`<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/<id>-<slug>`) must keep resolving to the worktree checkout, not the `--worklog-dir` parent (reuse `_same_git_repository`, audit_runner.py:770).
- Docs: skill/audit/SKILL.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md 'project scope is launch-cwd-only' claims must be rewritten.

## Problem statement

The audit runner auto-approves work items as "Ready to close: Yes" when `_extract_acs` returns the zero-AC sentinel (`["No acceptance criteria defined."]`) because it injects a hard-coded placeholder with `"verdict": "met"`. This creates a false-positive approval vector whenever an AC heading doesn't match the regex.

## Users

- **AI agents** running audits on work items (Ralph, AMPA) — expect the audit to accurately reflect AC verification status.
- **Operators** relying on "Ready to close: Yes" as a gating decision — assume ACs have been machine-verified.
- **User stories**:
  - "As an operator, I want the audit to never auto-approve an item with unverified ACs."
  - "As an AI agent, I want the audit to flag when AC extraction fails so I can review the item manually."

## Acceptance criteria

1. When `_extract_acs` returns the zero-AC sentinel, the runner emits a warning-level result and sets `Ready to close: No` (not Yes).
2. Existing items with valid AC headings still produce `Ready to close: Yes` (no regression on the happy path).
3. Unit test: `_extract_acs` sentinel path yields warning verdict.
4. Related documentation updated (code comments, any wiki/docs for the audit pipeline).
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the sentinel string returned by `_extract_acs` (backward compatibility with other callers).
- The fix is localized to the sentinel-handling branch in the audit runner (~line 5753).
- Should not require changes to the audit result schema (add `warning` level to existing verdict enum if needed).

## Existing state

- `_extract_acs` returns `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` on heading mismatch.
- The runner checks for this sentinel and injects `{"text": "No acceptance criteria defined.", "verdict": "met"}` (hard-coded placeholder).
- This produces "Ready to close: Yes" with zero ACs actually verified.
- Phase 2 deep analysis correctly detects the mismatch (separate safeguard) but the Phase 1 hard-coded sentinel still produces met verdict.

## Desired change

When the sentinel is detected, replace the hard-coded `{"verdict": "met"}` with a warning-level result (e.g. `{"verdict": "warning", "text": "ACs could not be extracted — verify item description uses a recognized heading format"}`). Ensure the overall verdict cannot be "Ready to close: Yes" when any result is warning-level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Sentinel handling branch (~line 5753)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — Add unit test for warning verdict on sentinel

## Related work

- SA-0MSM66WAQ001E0AX — audit_runner _extract_acs misses bold headings (source of discovery)
- SA-0MSJLC8XA00178YD — audit_runner AC extractor misses parenthetical headings (merged sibling fix)
- SA-0MSA843FV008V88P — _extract_acs fails on colon header (resolved, same root cause)

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q**: Should the zero-AC sentinel produce a `warning` verdict or a different handling (error/flag)? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: New `warning` verdict level. Source: code inspection — `warning` fits between `met` and `unmet` in severity.
- **Q**: Should Phase 1 or Phase 2 detect the sentinel path specifically? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: Phase 1 sentinel detection (~line 5753) is the primary fix point; Phase 2 already has a separate safeguard (detects 0 machine-verified ACs vs. description ACs). Source: code inspection of audit_runner.py.
- **Q**: Does this need to be a breaking schema change or can `warning` be additive? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: Additive — `warning` is a new enum value, backward-compatible. Source: code inspection — verdicts are string-based.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: The hard-coded placeholder at line 5753 is the sole place where `"verdict": "met"` is injected for the zero-AC sentinel. Other callers (child AC extraction at lines 4013, 4064) already skip processing when sentinel is detected — they do not produce a "Ready to close" verdict.
- **Risk**: Downstream consumers (Ralph, AMPA) may not yet handle a `warning` verdict level. Mitigation: additive enum value, not breaking; consumers that only check `met`/`unmet` will continue to work, treating `warning` conservatively.
- **Risk**: Adding "Ready to close: No" for sentinel paths may change audit results for existing items. Mitigation: these items already have a latent false-positive; the warning is a correction, not a regression.
- **Scope creep risk**: Consideration of auto-approving only when ACs are "sufficient" (count thresholds, content quality) is out of scope — this fix only addresses the sentinel→met path.

## Summary

Redirect all git-based audit operations (`_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, `_resolve_working_tree_hash`, `_compute_content_fingerprint`) to resolve against the worklog-derived owning project root instead of the launch cwd.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Git pieces target the owning project.** When the runner resolves an owning project root from the worklog (explicit `--worklog-dir` parent → prefix-to-sibling scan), `_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` resolve git against that root — **not** the launch cwd.

2. **Undeterminable ownership aborts.** When the owning project root cannot be determined (no `--worklog-dir`, unknown item prefix, no sibling match), the runner aborts with a clear error before any phase runs — it must not fall back to the launch cwd's repo for git-derived content.

3. **No regression for owning-project launches.** Launching from inside the owning project (standard path) and from a worktree of the owning project (same git repository) continues to work; a worktree launch still resolves git to the worktree checkout (never the `--worklog-dir` parent's main checkout), so worktree-only changes and the worktree branch HEAD stay correct.

## Implementation Details

**Approach: Pass `cwd` parameter to subprocess calls for git commands.**

The fix is to inject the owning project root as the `cwd` parameter when running git commands in the affected functions:

- `_git_changed_files(runner)` — modify calls to pass `cwd=str(git_root)` in `subprocess.run` (or wrap the runner to inject `cwd` for git commands).
- `_repo_index(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_resolve_audited_head(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_resolve_working_tree_hash(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_compute_content_fingerprint(runner)` — relies on the above, automatically fixed.
- `_build_file_scope_manifest(work_item, ac_results, runner)` — relies on `_git_changed_files` and `_repo_index`, automatically fixed.

**Recommended implementation strategy:**

Option A: Create a `cwd_aware_runner` wrapper function that prepends `-C <root>` to git commands, replacing `_default_runner` in the git-related calls. This is the simplest surgical change.

Option B: Modify `_default_runner` to accept an optional `cwd` parameter and create a `cwd_aware_runner` closure that pre-binds it. Update all git-related call sites to use `cwd_aware_runner(owning_root)` instead of `_default_runner`.

**Recommendation: Option A** — prepend `-C <root>` to git commands. It's a one-line change per function and avoids modifying the subprocess call signature.

```python
def _cwd_aware_runner(git_root: Path):
    """Return a runner function that prepends `-C <git_root>` to git commands."""
    def _run(cmd: Sequence[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        if cmd and cmd[0] == "git":
            cmd = ["git", "-C", str(git_root)] + list(cmd[1:])
        return _default_runner(cmd)
    return _run
```

**Abort on undeterminable ownership (AC2):**

In `cmd_issue()` (around line 5377), after resolving `owning_root`, if it is `None`, abort with a clear error message before any git operations run. The existing `_verify_launch_context` currently fails open (returns `None` when ownership is undeterminable); this fix turns the abort into the git layer's responsibility.

**Worktree semantics (AC3):**

Reuse the existing `_same_git_repository` logic (line 767). When `owning_root` is resolved and the launch cwd is the same git repository (via `_same_git_repository`), use the launch cwd as the git root. Otherwise use the resolved `owning_root`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_git_changed_files` (:2953), `_repo_index` (:2983), `_resolve_audited_head` (:1348), `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (:1080), `cmd_issue` (5377+).

# Pre-existing dev blockers: eslint missing, context-budget exceeded, audit-runner failures

## Problem statement

Three pre-existing failures block ALL `dev` pushes via the pre-push gate (test gate SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 + context-budget gate SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY). They were discovered while pushing SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR (skill_path shim) and reproduced on the clean `dev` base (`c8a38a8`). No code from SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR causes them.

## Users

- **Agent/Developer pushing to `dev`** — wants `git push` to pass the pre-push gate (tests + `measure_context.py --thresholds`) without triaging unrelated failures. *Story: As a developer pushing a feature to dev, I want the pre-push gate to be green on a clean checkout so I can land my change without unrelated blockers.*
- **CI / Release Manager** — wants the full project test suite green and context-budget thresholds consistent so the `dev → main` ship gate can proceed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Context-budget gate passes:** `python3 skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py --repo-root . --thresholds docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` exits 0 (no thresholds exceeded). Thresholds reflect the approved startup budget including the hygiene guidance added in 80dbf5a2.
2. **ESLint ESM-parsing tests pass or skip cleanly:** `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eslint_esm_parsing.py -q` is green — either 18 passed when `eslint` is available, or skipped/xfail with a clear message when the binary is absent (no `FileNotFoundError` hard failure).
3. **Audit-runner persist/review suites pass:** `python3 -m pytest tests/test_audit_runner_persist.py tests/test_audit_runner_review.py tests/test_audit_runner_core.py -q` is green on a clean checkout (no stale-cache or environment flake).
4. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (`python3 -m pytest -q` or `skill/test` harness green, excluding only explicitly skipped env-dependent tests).
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (docs/dev/context-budget.md thresholds table if thresholds change).

## Constraints

- Do not regress startup context beyond the approved hygiene addition; any increase must be reflected in committed thresholds.
- Pre-push hook (`skill/context-audit` + test gate) must remain enforcing — no disabling or bypassing gates.
- Fixes must be environment-robust (e.g., eslint-missing skip) so CI and fresh clones are green without manual setup.

## Existing state

- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` = `{global:8192, project:1334, skills_prose:3523, total:13049}` — stale. Current measurement (`--repo-root .`) = `global 8335 (+143), project 1723 (+389), skills_prose 1168 (-2355), total 11226 (-1823)`. Gate fails on `global_agents` and `project_agents` (verified `EXIT 2` on HEAD).
- `tests/test_eslint_esm_parsing.py` previously failed with 8× `FileNotFoundError: 'eslint'` when `node_modules/.bin/eslint` absent. Current HEAD re-run: **18 passed** (likely fixed by a3b0d886/8db22abc or env now provides eslint) — verify and harden with skip logic if needed.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_persist.py` / `test_audit_runner_review.py` / `test_audit_runner_core.py` previously failed on clean dev base (cache staleness). Current HEAD re-run: **222 passed** — verify stability and ensure no cache-dependent flake.
- Commit 80dbf5a2 (SA-0MT4DFE8Y004J8SP "Add stash hygiene gate") is on `dev`; thresholds were not bumped when AGENTS files grew.

## Desired change

- **Context budget:** Regenerate and commit `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from current measurement (`python3 skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py --repo-root . --generate-thresholds`) — proposed `{8335, 1723, 1168, 11226}` — and update `docs/dev/context-budget.md` baseline notes if needed. Alternative (if producer prefers): trim AGENTS_GLOBAL.md/AGENTS.md hygiene pointers to fit old thresholds; default is threshold bump since hygiene content is intentional and small.
- **ESLint:** Ensure `test_eslint_esm_parsing.py` skips cleanly when `eslint` binary absent (e.g., `pytest.skip` / `shutil.which` guard) so missing env does not hard-fail the suite; keep passing when eslint present.
- **Audit runner:** Confirm persist/review failures are resolved on HEAD; if any residual cache/flake remains, fix test isolation (cache clear, tmp isolation, or `test_cache` staleness handling) so suites are deterministic.
- Re-verify pre-push gate end-to-end (tests + `measure_context.py --thresholds`) and full suite green before closing.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — Stale thresholds causing gate failure; needs regeneration.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — Measurement tool; verify `--repo-root` and `--thresholds` behavior.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — Baseline documentation; update if thresholds change.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (8335 B) / `AGENTS.md` (1723 B) — Grew in 80dbf5a2; sizes vs thresholds.
- `tests/test_eslint_esm_parsing.py` — Previously 8 failures on missing eslint; needs skip guard.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_persist.py`, `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py`, `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`, `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`, `skill/test` harness — Suites to verify green.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Hygiene content that grew AGENTS files.

## Related work

- **Discovered-from:** SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR (skill_path shim) — context where blockers were reported.
- **Context-budget gate:** SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY (regression gate F6), SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP (baseline), SA-0MT4DFE8Y004J8SP / commit 80dbf5a2 (stash hygiene gate that grew AGENTS files and exceeded thresholds).
- **ESLint:** SA-0MSNS6DMK002KLFR ([test-failure] eslint binary missing, completed), SA-0MSQ5XQNZ002XM5Q (test_eslint_esm_parsing failure, completed), SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC (pre-existing fixes).
- **Audit runner:** SA-0MPDXZ5OX009K1B1 / SA-0MPDXYG3J001YQF3 (audit_runner core), SA-0MQ00W5BX002HAHT (persistence robustness), SA-0MSRMFXAQ002CE13 (verification — blocked).
- **Ship/release gating:** SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 (test gate), SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY (context-budget gate).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Bumping thresholds hides future budget creep. *Mitigation:* Bump only by the measured hygiene delta (+143/+389) and tighten `skills_prose`/`total` downward; document in `context-budget.md`; keep gate enforcing.
- **Risk:** eslint-available vs missing env divergence causes CI-only failures. *Mitigation:* Add explicit `shutil.which("eslint")` skip with clear message; test both paths.
- **Risk:** Audit-runner cache staleness recurs on fresh clones. *Mitigation:* Ensure tests use isolated tmp/cache or clear stale fixtures; verify on clean worktree.
- **Assumption:** Hygiene guidance in AGENTS files is intentional and approved — threshold bump is preferred over trimming content. If producer prefers trimming, adjust AGENTS files instead.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not expand into broader pre-push refactoring; record any extra opportunities (e.g., broader eslint env setup, broader context-budget trimming) as linked follow-up work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the context-budget fix bump thresholds to the current measurement or trim AGENTS_GLOBAL.md/AGENTS.md back under the old thresholds?" — Answer (assumed, pending producer confirmation): Bump thresholds to generated values `{global:8335, project:1723, skills_prose:1168, total:11226}` since the hygiene addition (≈5 lines + 1 line) is intentional and small, and `skills_prose`/`total` actually shrink, tightening the overall budget. Source: measurement on HEAD (`measure_context.py --repo-root . --generate-thresholds`) and diff of 80dbf5a2. If producer prefers trimming, replace with AGENTS file compression and keep old thresholds.
- Q: "Are the eslint and audit-runner failures still reproducible on HEAD, or have they been fixed by intervening commits?" — Answer (research, 2026-09-01): Re-ran on HEAD — `test_eslint_esm_parsing.py` now 18 passed; `test_audit_runner_*` now 222 passed. Indicates intervening fixes resolved them, but hardening (eslint skip guard, cache isolation) is still warranted to prevent recurrence on clean envs. Source: `python3 -m pytest` runs in this session.

The audit skill's Phase 1 merge gate (_integrate_into_dev in skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, ~lines 6099-6109) unconditionally runs 'npm run build' after merging the item's work into an integration worktree (build -> test -> commit order per AGENTS.md). For a repo without package.json / build tooling (e.g. docs-only repos such as AI_Hell), this fails with ENOENT and the gate reports 'Merge gate blocked: integration failed: build failed' -> 'Ready to close: No', demoting the item to open/plan_complete — even though the git merge itself succeeded (rc=0) and the change is valid.

User story: As an operator auditing a docs-only work item in a repo without build tooling, I want the audit merge gate to skip/soften the build step so valid changes can pass Phase 1 without the workaround of committing+pushing to dev first.

Impact: any docs-only item in a repo without build tooling cannot pass the audit merge gate when the work is not yet in dev. Workaround (used for AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V): commit + push to dev FIRST, then audit — _verify_merged_in_dev detects the work already in origin/dev and fails open without attempting the build.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Have an audited work item whose commits are NOT yet in origin/dev.
2. Run the audit on a repo with no package.json (e.g. a docs-only GDD repo).
3. Observe the Phase 1 merge gate fail with 'build error'/'build failed' despite the merge succeeding.

Suggested fix: make the build step conditional on the integration worktree having package.json (or a configured build command, e.g. .pi/test-config.json buildCommand), or record a non-blocking note when no build tooling exists. Mirror the conditional-skip approach already applied to the implement skill's run_build() (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1) and run_tests() (SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Audit Phase 1 integration succeeds for a repo with no package.json and no build tooling; the build step is skipped and recorded as evidence (non-blocking note), not a failure.
2. Audit Phase 1 still runs 'npm run build' and fails the gate when a package.json with a build script exists and the build fails.
3. Existing merge-gate tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py and related) remain green; a new test covers the no-build-tooling case.
4. Behavior is consistent with the implement skill's conditional build/test skip conventions (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1, SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

## Bug Report: implement skill report script path is broken

### Problem

The implement skill's final end-of-session report step references a report script at a path that does not exist in this repository.

### Expected Path

```
$(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py
```

This resolves to:
```
/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py
```

### Actual Result

The file does not exist:
```
python3: can't open file '/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

### Impact

- The implement skill's end-of-session report cannot be generated automatically
- Agents fall back to manual report rendering
- The `render_report.py` script may exist in the shared skills directory but is not found via `skill_path report`

### Required Fix

1. Verify the report skill location and script path
2. Update the implement skill's `SKILL.md` to reference the correct path
3. Or create the missing script at the expected location
4. Or update `skill_path report` to resolve to the correct directory

### References

- Implement skill: `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md` (Step: "Final step: standardized end-of-session report")
- Report skill reference: `../report/SKILL.md` within implement skill

---

## Root Cause (corrected during planning)

The original report's "Expected Path" is inaccurate. Verified during planning (2026-09-18):

- `$(skill_path report)` is resolved at runtime by the `skill_path` **shell shim** (`scripts/skill_path`), not by the pi `skill_path` tool. The shim mirrors the tool's search order and must be installed at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` (first on `PATH`).
- `render_report.py` **exists and runs** — it lives in the `report` skill's own directory, not in the implement skill:
  ```
  $ bash scripts/skill_path report
  /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report
  $ python3 "$(bash scripts/skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py" --help   # exits 0
  ```
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to this repo's `skill/` tree.)
- **The defect:** the shim is **not installed** at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`. `~/.pi/agent/bin` is first on `PATH` but contains only `fd` and `rg`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `skill/`, `command/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and installs config + the pre-push hook, but **never installs the shim** — so `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` is missing on every machine that has run the installer.
- **Consequence:** `$(skill_path report)` expands to nothing in bash, so the documented command fails. The implement skill's `SKILL.md` invocation string (`$(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py`) is **already correct**; **no path edit to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is required**.
- The shim was added in commit `ed2c25e8` (SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR) whose message/docs claim it is "installed at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`", but no install wiring shipped and the file is committed with mode `100644` (not executable).

## Required Fix (corrected)

1. `scripts/install_pi.sh`: install `scripts/skill_path` to `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` (`mkdir -p`, copy/install, `chmod +x`), idempotently; warn (fail-open, non-fatal) if `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin` is not on `PATH`.
2. Commit `scripts/skill_path` as executable (`100755`).
3. Install the shim on this machine and verify the implement skill's documented final-step command runs end-to-end from the project CWD.
4. Add a regression test so the missing-install defect cannot recur.
5. Update `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` to state that `install_pi.sh` installs the shim and that `~/.pi/agent/bin` must be on `PATH`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the implement skill's documented final-step command verbatim from a project CWD renders the canonical report (exit 0, all report sections present) — no manual path resolution.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs `scripts/skill_path` to `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` as an executable, and a re-run is idempotent (shim intact, script exits 0).
- `skill_path <name>` resolves to the correct directory for every installed skill, and exits non-zero with a clear error message for an unknown skill.
- A regression test asserts the shim install wiring and resolution behaviour, so the defect cannot recur undetected.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` states that `install_pi.sh` installs the shim and lists the `~/.pi/agent/bin` PATH prerequisite; the implement skill's documented invocation remains unchanged and is executed verbatim in the AC1 verification.

## Scope

**In scope:** install wiring for the `skill_path` shim in `scripts/install_pi.sh`; executable mode for `scripts/skill_path`; installing the shim on this machine; regression test; docs note.

**Out of scope:** changing the `$(skill_path <name>)/scripts/...` convention; editing `skill/implement/SKILL.md` or `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (both already correct); moving `render_report.py`; changing the report template or the report-wiring hygiene tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the reported "Expected Path" (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py`) match reality?
  Answer (planning, verified by investigation): No. `skill_path report` resolves to the `report` skill directory (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report`), where `render_report.py` already exists and runs. The implement skill's own `scripts/` directory has no `report/` subdir. Evidence: `bash scripts/skill_path report`, `python3 "$(bash scripts/skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py" --help`.
- Q: Why did the command fail if the script exists?
  Answer (planning, verified): the `skill_path` shell shim is not installed at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`, so bash command substitution `$(skill_path report)` produces no path. `scripts/install_pi.sh` has no shim-install step. Evidence: `ls ~/.pi/agent/bin` (only `fd`, `rg`); `grep -n skill_path scripts/install_pi.sh` (no match); docs claim the shim is installed.
- Q: Which fix option (edit `implement/SKILL.md`, create a script, or fix `skill_path` resolution) should be taken?
  Answer (planning, decided on evidence): install the shim via `install_pi.sh`. The `implement/SKILL.md` invocation is already correct, the renderer already exists, and the shim already resolves `report` correctly — only the installation wiring is missing. Editing the SKILL.md path would contradict the documented convention and the `test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` guard.
- No open questions requiring producer input; the auto-complete (skip) determination is Extra Small effort / Low risk.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — add shim installation block (copy + chmod +x + PATH warning).
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — report renderer (existing; expected unchanged).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — final-step invocation (existing; expected unchanged — verify only).
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — document install wiring + PATH prerequisite.
- `tests/test_install_pi_skill_path_shim.py` — new regression test (sandboxed install + resolution).
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — existing guard; must continue to pass.

The shim source is `scripts/skill_path` (extensionless by design; installed to `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`). It is expected to remain behaviourally unchanged and should be committed with executable mode `100755`.

## Problem

The audit runner's merge gate (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) extracts candidate commit SHAs from work-item descriptions and comments using the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`. This regex incorrectly matches decimal numbers that happen to be composed entirely of hex digits (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` from a test failure message). The numeric sequence after the decimal point (`2329094824319696`, `231051271500847`) is treated as a valid commit SHA, causing false-positive merge-gate failures.

**Example:** A failing test with the error:
```
expected 0.23290948243196963 to be less than or equal to 0.2310512715008475
```
produces candidate commits `2329094824319696` and `231051271500847` from the audit runner, which then fail to integrate into `dev` because they are not real commit SHAs.

## Root Cause

File: `.pi/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`, line ~6119:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

The `\b` word boundary does not prevent matching within decimal numbers. The sequence `0.23290948243196963` is parsed as a decimal literal, but the substring `2329094824319696` (16 hex chars) passes the 7-40 char hex check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit no longer extracts decimal numbers as commit SHAs:** The regex in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` must not match numeric sequences that are part of decimal literals (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` → no SHA extracted; `2329094824319696` → no SHA extracted).

2. **Valid commit SHAs are still extracted:** The fix must not break extraction of legitimate commit SHAs:
   - Full 40-hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd3cc78f415afca198930339f2138bed218`)
   - Short 7-39 hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd`, `abc1234`)
   - SHAs in commit messages, WL comment text, and work-item descriptions

3. **Commit SHAs prefixed by `#` (GitHub-style) are still extracted:** `#2c15ebd` or `sha=2c15ebd` patterns should still be detected (the `\b` boundary handles `#` as a non-word character, so the hex sequence is still matched).

4. **All existing audit tests pass:** No regression in the existing audit test suite (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/`).

5. **New test coverage:** Add a test that verifies decimal numbers are not extracted as commit SHAs, and a test that verifies valid SHAs in various formats (full, short, GitHub-style) are still extracted.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b` with one that excludes decimal-point-adjacent sequences. Options:

**Option A (negative lookbehind for dot):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!\.)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?!\.)", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This uses `(?<!\.)` to ensure the match is not preceded by a decimal point, and `(?!\.)` to ensure it is not followed by one.

**Option B (explicit non-digit-dot context):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![0-9.])\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?![0-9.])", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This is more aggressive — it excludes any sequence preceded or followed by digits or dots.

**Option C (split on dots first, then match):**
Preprocess the text: `text.replace('.', ' ')`, then apply the original regex. This is simpler but could break SHAs that happen to be adjacent to dots in unusual contexts (unlikely but possible in commit messages).

**Recommended:** Option A — targeted fix that only excludes decimal-point adjacency, preserving all other behavior.

## Impact

- **Scope:** Single function in `audit_runner.py` (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`)
- **Risk:** Low — the change is a regex refinement; behavior is identical for all real commit SHAs.
- **Test coverage:** Existing audit tests cover SHA extraction from descriptions and comments; add a test for decimal exclusion.

## Related Work

- N/A — this is a bug in the audit skill's core merge-gate logic.

# Pane title status indicator on skill completion

## Problem statement

When a skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, …) finishes, the operator
cannot tell at a glance whether the pane's work-item session ended cleanly,
needs their attention, or failed. The herdr pane title currently shows only
the dispatch context (e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); the end-of-session
state must be surfaced in the pane title itself.

## Users

- **Operator (producer)** watching a grid of herdr panes: wants a zero-click
  visual signal of which sessions are done, need attention, or failed —
  without opening each pane.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when a skill completes cleanly I want a green tick at the
  start of the pane title so I can see it finished."
- "As an operator, when a skill completes but left information for my
  attention I want an orange warning so I know to look at it."
- "As an operator, when a skill cannot complete I want a red no-entry sign
  so I know to intervene."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a work-item skill finishes and produces a final report, the herdr
  pane title (label) for the current pane is updated with a status prefix:
  ✅ (or `Done`) when all ACs are met and no substantive producer content
  exists; ⚠️ (or `Note`) when the skill completed but the report contains
  substantive content for the producer's attention; 🚫 (or `Attention`) when
  the skill cannot complete (any unmet/partial/adjusted AC verdict, or
  abort/failure).
- AC2: The prefix is prepended to the existing pane title (e.g.
  `✅ Manually triggered intake`); no colour/ANSI is embedded in the label;
  the update is idempotent (re-running does not stack prefixes).
- AC3: Text fallbacks `Done` / `Note` / `Attention` are used when emoticons
  are not possible (reusing the report's existing `--no-icons` /
  `WL_NO_ICONS=1` mechanism).
- AC4: On skill abort or failure (including abort paths such as
  `intake.py abort`, `implement.py abort`, audit-runner aborts), the pane
  title is set to the red state regardless of whether a final report is
  produced.
- AC5: The update fails gracefully outside a herdr pane (no `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or herdr CLI unavailable): no crash, no error surfaced to
  the skill run.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and all
  related documentation is updated (SKILL.md reports, tests for the new
  helper).

## Constraints

- Not a pi extension — the update is a call to the herdr CLI/API
  (`herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane id from
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; herdr ≥ current installed version).
- Trigger is skill completion (end-of-session report render), not the agent
  harness lifecycle.
- Status is derived from the final report's content: AC verdicts
  (met/unmet/adjusted/partial), Producer Actions, Notes.
- Orange = "audit passed but there is information for the producer's
  attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action
  is the standard next action in the workflow)" — i.e. substantive content
  beyond the routine workflow next step.
- Colour requirement dropped for text fallbacks: plain `Done`/`Note`/
  `Attention` prefixes, no colour coding.
- Emoji-vs-text fallback follows the existing report convention
  (`--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1`), so both modes stay consistent.

## Existing state

- Every work-item skill ends by rendering a canonical report via
  `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (report skill, SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S),
  passing AC verdicts, producer actions, notes and next action.
- herdr panes carry a `label` field shown as the pane title, set via
  `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane is identified by the
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var (present in pi sessions launched via herdr; also
  `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `render_report.py` already supports `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` for
  bracketed-text fallbacks — a precedent for the emoticon/text switch.

## Desired change

- Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`) that, given a
  status (`done` | `note` | `attention`) and the current pane context,
  prepends the corresponding prefix (✅/⚠️/🚫 or Done/Note/Attention) to the
  existing pane label via the herdr CLI, idempotently.
- Integrate the helper into `render_report.py`: after the report is rendered,
  derive the status from the supplied AC verdicts, producer actions and notes
  and update the pane title (done/note states; red when any AC verdict is not
  met).
- Hook the red state into abort paths (`intake.py abort`, `implement.py
  abort`, audit runner abort/exit paths) so failures always surface red even
  without a final report.
- Fail open when not in a herdr pane or herdr CLI is missing.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — derive status from report inputs
  and call the pane-title helper after rendering.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (new) — shared herdr CLI wrapper: resolve
  current pane, read existing label, prepend status prefix idempotently.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — abort command sets red pane state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — abort path sets red pane state.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — abort/failure exits set red pane
  state.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` + `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` —
  document and test the status derivation and pane update.

## Risks & assumptions

- **herdr CLI availability:** assume herdr is installed and the pane env vars
  are set in agent panes (true today — pi sessions launched via herdr carry
  `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`). Fail-open behaviour (AC5) mitigates drift.
- **Existing pane title truncation:** herdr truncates long labels to ~60
  chars (`MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH`); the prefix plus existing label must fit
  within the limit — the helper should truncate the combined string the same
  way to keep the title valid.
- **Scope creep:** wiring red-state into *every* skill's abort path is broad;
  the helper centralises the logic so each abort site is a one-liner. Extra
  opportunities (e.g. coloured labels in the herdr UI itself) are recorded as
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Verdict vocabulary:** `adjusted`/`partial` verdicts count as "not fully
  met" → red; `met` only → eligible for done/note.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill": the report renderer this feature extends.
- ContextHub herdr (sibling repo `packages/herdr`): `pane rename`, pane
  titles (`pane-title.ts`, WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), agent-state protocol.
- find-related matches (repo): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the
  abort/failure paths that must surface the red state; no directly-related
  open work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should this live in the SorraAgents repo as a reusable extension, or be a built-in feature in the pi-coding-agent?" — Answer (user): "It is not a pi extension, it is a call to the herdr CLI/API." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q: "Should the title update happen on agent_settled or agent_end?" — Answer (user): "Triggers by the completion of a skill, not by the agent harness." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "To detect a producer notification, check needsProducerReview?" — Answer (user): "The final summary from the skill indicates status." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the complete title look like?" — Answer (user): "Just add the prefix to the existing title." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which herdr command sets the pane title?" — Answer (user): "Don't know — look it up using herdr --help." Research: `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>` sets the pane label (pane list `label` field, e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); current pane id from `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; `herdr pane report-metadata --title` is display-only metadata (not the label). Accepted answer: `herdr pane rename` with `HERDR_PANE_ID`.
- Q: "Status derivation from the final summary?" — Answer (user): "Green is correct; Orange is audit passed but there is information for the producer's attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action is the standard next action in the workflow); Red is correct." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where should the herdr call live?" — Answer (user): "(a) inside render_report.py so every skill gets it automatically." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Orange trigger precision — substantive content?" — Answer (user): "Substantive content." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Red path for aborts?" — Answer (user): "Always show red." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Fallback colour mechanics?" — Answer (user): "Drop the colour requirement." Source: interactive reply.
