# Intake Brief: Always mark items as in_progress while an agent is working on them (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9)

## Problem Statement

Agents must hold `status: in_progress` for the entire duration they are actively working on a work item. During the 2026-08-30 incident, a plan run released AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC to `open` at 12:08:51Z to pause for producer approval and never re-claimed after approval at 12:09:42Z, leaving the item `open` while creating children and updating descriptions until 12:18:40Z — allowing the herdr downtime worker to legitimately dispatch a duplicate `/skill:plan` at 12:13:02Z.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the worklog to truthfully show whether an item is claimed, so downtime dispatch never duplicates work that is already in progress.
  - *Story:* As an operator, I want any active agent workflow to hold `in_progress` so `wl next` and the downtime worker do not re-dispatch the same item.
- **Agent (plan/intake/implement/audit/effort-and-risk)** — needs a clear, enforced lifecycle so pause/resume and error paths cannot silently leave an item `open` while mutations continue.
  - *Story:* As an agent running plan, after producer approval resumes my run I want the re-claim to be automatic/required before any child creation or description update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Plan skill re-claims `status: in_progress` immediately after producer approval resumes a paused run, before any further work (child creation, dep wiring, description/comment updates); verified by a test driving the approval-gate flow where the item is `in_progress` continuously from approval through completion and never `open` in that window.
- [ ] No agent process performs work-item mutations (create children, update description, wire deps, completion comments) while `status: open`; SKILL.md files for plan, intake, implement, audit, and effort-and-risk are reviewed and updated to enforce claim-before-work and re-claim-after-any-pause, with any remaining `release to open while work continues` patterns eliminated or explicitly documented as handoff-only.
- [ ] A downtime-dispatched plan run that hits the approval gate with no interactive user does not release the item to `open` while the run remains active (holds claim or aborts cleanly).
- [ ] StatusLifecycle (shared helper) provides a mechanism to assert/automate re-claim on resume (e.g. `require_claimed` guard and/or `on_resume` re-claim), with unit tests covering the pause→approval→re-claim path and the guard failure when work is attempted on `open`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; `wl sync` is clean.

## Constraints

- Must not introduce orphaned `in_progress` items: every claim has a matching terminal release (`open`/`blocked`/`completed`) on completion, error/abort, or genuine session handoff.
- `completed` status remains compatible only with `in_review`/`done` stages (wl CLI validation); skills that restore on exit must not force `completed` on `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`.
- Worklog-dir resolution must remain correct regardless of caller cwd (reuse `run_wl`/`resolve_worklog_flags`, prefix-to-sibling scan).
- Change is to agent framework (SorraAgents) — affects every project once installed via `scripts/install_pi.sh`; needs work-item tracking, tests, and push to `dev`.

## Existing State

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` line 42 specifies claim-first via `StatusLifecycle.update_status(<id>, "in_progress")` and line 47 specifies "Pausing for producer input" → `update_status(<id>, "open", needs_producer_review=True)`. The manual run at 2026-08-30T12:08:51Z followed the pause-release but never re-claimed after approval at 12:09:42Z before creating 3 children at 12:11:28Z.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` provides `StatusLifecycle` context manager and `update_status`/`show`/`run_wl` helpers with worklog-dir injection; no `require_claimed` guard or resume re-claim helper exists yet.
- Other skills (intake, implement, audit, effort-and-risk) have varying lifecycle adherence; previous migrations (SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ, SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO) wired StatusLifecycle into some skills but not uniformly.
- Downtime worker dispatches `critical + open + intake_complete` candidates via CAS (`--if-status open --if-stage intake_complete`), so any `open` window during active work is a duplicate-dispatch hazard.

## Desired Change

- Enforce invariant: **actively worked => `in_progress`; released to `open` only at true handoff** (completion, error/abort, or session actually ending).
- Plan skill: after producer approval, immediately re-claim `in_progress` before any work-bearing step; add a guard that the item is `in_progress` before child creation/dep wiring/description updates.
- SKILL.md guidance: clarify that pause-release applies only when the session hands control back for an open-ended wait with no in-session resume; approval-resume must re-claim.
- Shared helper: add `require_claimed(id)` and/or `on_resume` re-claim flow used by skills before mutations.
- Downtime plan runs hitting the approval gate hold the claim (keep `in_progress`) or abort cleanly — never release to `open` mid-run.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Clarify pause vs. handoff semantics; require re-claim after approval before any work.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — Approval-gate and plan-if-needed helpers; ensure they re-claim or hold claim.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Add `require_claimed` guard and/or resume re-claim helper; add tests.
- `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — Extend with pause→approval→re-claim and guard tests.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work and re-claim-after-pause compliance.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work compliance.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Verify claim-before-work compliance.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — Verify restore_on_exit vs. claim semantics.
- `README.md` — Agent Status Lifecycle section documenting the in_progress invariant (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9).

## Related Work

- Potentially related work items:
  - SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ — Implement and plan skills don't use StatusLifecycle context manager (completed)
  - SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO — Wire shared StatusLifecycle into implementall, intakeall, planall (completed)
  - SA-0MS93J0ZC007IO8V — Skill scripts rely on caller cwd for wl and force status=completed (completed)
  - SA-0MS31SAM20004GTJ — All actions should leave the status in a good state (completed)
  - SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF — When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing (in_progress) — related downtime/idle-gate interaction
  - SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 — This item (root cause: AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC at 2026-08-30T12:13:02.827Z duplicate dispatch; manual plan session 2026-08-30T12-03-10-333Z)
- Potentially related docs:
  - `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared lifecycle helper (source of invariant enforcement)
  - `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Plan skill claim/pause lifecycle (lines 42, 47, 112)
  - `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — Plan implementation reference
  - `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — Intake reference (worklog resolution, issue type guide)
  - `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — Worklog sync and worklog-dir resolution

## Risks & Assumptions

- Risk: Over-eager re-claim could mask genuine handoffs and leave items stuck `in_progress` visible as orphaned. Mitigation: re-claim only on in-session resume; terminal release still required on completion/error/abort.
- Risk: `wl` CAS dispatch relies on `open` to find candidates; holding `in_progress` longer reduces dispatch surface but may starve other work if claim is held too long. Mitigation: scope claim to actual work duration; no change to dispatch query.
- Risk: Existing skills without StatusLifecycle coverage may regress. Mitigation: audit all five skills and add guards/tests.
- Assumption: Producer approval in interactive pane is in-session resume (not handoff) — validated by incident timeline.
- Assumption: Downtime worker has no interactive approver; holding claim is preferred to releasing to `open`. Needs validation with herdr/downtime code.
- Scope-creep risk: Generalizing to a repo-wide status invariant could expand to queue/dispatch policy changes — record as linked follow-ups, not in-scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Who is the primary user for this invariant?" — Answer (inferred from description): Operator and agent workflows; operator wants truthful claimed state, agents need enforced lifecycle. Source: work item description Goals/user story. No new interview needed — brief is well-defined.
- Q: "Should downtime-dispatched runs ever release to open mid-run?" — Answer (from description): No — hold claim or abort cleanly. Source: description Required behaviour #4 and Suggested implementation. OPEN QUESTION retained for herdr/downtime implementation detail: confirm preferred abort vs. hold behavior with herdr maintainer if code path differs.
- Q: "Does this duplicate SA-0MS69FE4Q008N8SZ / SA-0MS1MQ8GF002YXZO?" — Answer: No — those wired StatusLifecycle into skills; this item fixes the pause→resume re-claim gap those did not cover (incident at 12:08:51Z–12:11:28Z). Source: wl search and description root cause recap. Research: searched work items for StatusLifecycle/plan skill; prior items completed without resume guard.

## Goal

Make the audit freshness-skip output explicit and actionable so that when a session encounters a fresh audit, it immediately sees the verdict and age — no need to parse the rawOutput.

## Background

When `_check_audit_freshness` returns a fresh report (content fingerprint unchanged), the runner prints:

Skipping: audit still fresh
<existing report>

This is terse. AC2 requires that the runner *surfaces an existing fresh audit* with the verdict and auditedAt timestamp. The fix is to add a structured summary line before the raw output.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a fresh audit is detected, the skip output includes a line like:
   `Skipping: audit fresh — Ready to close: Yes (auditedAt: <ISO timestamp>)`
   (or `Ready to close: No` depending on the verdict).

2. The auditedAt timestamp is included so the operator can judge freshness at a glance.

3. The rawOutput is still printed after the summary line (no data loss).

## Key Files:
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (skip block around cmd_issue)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (freshness gate section — verify message documented)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (test for skip message)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (freshness integration test)

## Deliverables
- Minimal code change in the skip block
- Updated test confirming skip message format

## Goal

Prove AC4: auditing an item twice at the same HEAD short-circuits the second run — the fresh audit is reused and the model is NOT invoked.

## Background

The freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness`) already returns the stored report when the content fingerprint (HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state) is unchanged. The `test_freshness_skip_performs_no_transitions` test in `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` covers the lifecycle aspect with a mocked freshness result. AC4 wants a test that audits twice at the same HEAD and asserts the second run short-circuits without invoking the model.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A test creates a work item with an existing fresh audit report (content fingerprint matching current state), then runs `cmd_issue` again at the same HEAD.

2. The second run returns exit code 0 and does NOT invoke the model (no pi calls — assert via mock that the Pi runner/`_call_pi` is never called, or via a fake model that would raise if invoked).

3. The test asserts that `_check_audit_freshness` returned the stored rawOutput (fresh path taken).

4. The test is deterministic — no timing dependence (uses explicit fingerprint computation, not the 60s time gate).

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (fallback placement if needed)

## Goal

Create a file-based, cross-process bounded priority queue module in `skill/shared/` that supports priority ordering (critical > high > medium > low > FIFO/age within tier) and crash recovery (via flock semantics — no stale locks).

## Problem

The existing `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` counts slots but has no ordering guarantee — a new process can grab a free slot before an older waiter (no priority or FIFO). Audits starve the oldest items indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Priority ordering:** items enqueued with priority `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` are dequeued in priority order (critical first, then high, then medium, then low); within the same priority tier, FIFO/age ordering is observed.
2. **Bounded capacity:** the queue has a configurable maximum depth (default 50); enqueuing beyond capacity blocks (or returns a bounded-wait result) rather than growing unboundedly.
3. **Crash recovery:** no stale queue state after process crash — kernel flock semantics guarantee no stale locks; orphaned entries are detected by TTL or directory scan and cleaned on next enqueue.
4. **Cross-process safety:** the module works correctly under concurrent enqueue/dequeue from independent processes (same flock-based no-stale-lock design as the semaphore).
5. **Unit tests:** `skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py` covers ordering, bounded capacity, crash recovery, and concurrent access (≥ 80% coverage).
6. **No regression to process_semaphore.py:** the existing semaphore module is untouched; the queue is a separate module.

## Implementation Details

- **File:** `skill/shared/queue.py` (new)
- **Lock directory:** `/<name>/` (reuse existing infrastructure)
- **Queue format:** JSON files with `{priority, timestamp, item_id}` keys; directory listing sorted by priority then timestamp gives dequeue order
- **Capacity enforcement:** bounded with blocking wait (configurable timeout)
- **Cleanup:** orphan entries > TTL (default 24h) are removed on read; also a periodic scan

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/queue.py` — new module
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — existing semaphore (unchanged, for reference)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py` — unit tests (new),

data.description:
## Goal

Replace the audit runner's 0s fail-fast semaphore acquisition with the bounded priority queue (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L), so audits wait in a prioritized queue instead of failing with "Audit concurrency limit reached" unmet verdicts.

## Problem

`_acquire_audit_slot()` in `audit_runner.py` passes `timeout=0` (fail-fast) to the semaphore. Under saturated concurrency, every audit returns unmet immediately — wasting model time on re-trials and keeping items stuck in `in_review` indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Zero fail-fast unmet verdicts:** under sustained concurrent agent/LLM traffic, audits no longer return unmet "Audit concurrency limit reached". Instead, they wait in the priority queue and acquire a slot when one becomes free. Verification: run N >= 3 concurrent audits against a busy host; zero concurrency-limit unmet verdicts; all audits persist real verdicts.

2. **Priority ordering enforced:** among queued audit candidates, critical items are audited before high, then medium, then low; within the same priority tier, FIFO/age ordering is observed.

3. **Bounded wait with queue:** the audit runner enqueues itself with its work-item priority; when the queue capacity is full, it waits (bounded, not fail-fast) until space opens.

4. **Observability — queue logging:** each audit logs its queue position, priority, and estimated wait time; on completion, the total time-queued is recorded. Logs include: queued_at=<ts>, priority=<level>, queue_position=<N>, dequeued_at=<ts>, wait_seconds=<N>.

5. **No regression to existing guards:** per-item in_progress claim guard, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight, lease/leader machinery, and test-cache read-only consumption all continue to work unchanged.

6. **Integration tests:** `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` covers the queue-aware audit launch, priority ordering, and no-fail-fast behavior under saturation.

## Implementation

- **File:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — modify `_acquire_audit_slot()` to use the shared queue instead of bare semaphore acquire
- **Change location:** ~line 2124 (_acquire_audit_slot), ~line 2796 (the with _acquire_audit_slot(): call site)
- **Priority resolution:** derive item priority from the work item's priority field (critical > high > medium > low)
- **Logging:** use existing audit logging infrastructure to record queue metrics

## Dependencies

- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (shared priority queue module must be created first)

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_acquire_audit_slot()` (2124), `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (134-135)
- `skill/shared/queue.py` — new shared queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` — integration tests (new)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — update concurrency documentation

## Sequencing Note

## Goal

When the idle gate does open (rare under sustained traffic), the audit runner should process multiple queued items in priority order within a single dispatch window instead of auditing one item per window. This multiplies per-window throughput and drains the backlog faster.

## Problem

With the bounded queue (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM), each audit still waits for a slot individually. If the gate opens every 30 minutes, that is one audit per 30 minutes. A batch drain processes N items in sequence within one window, releasing and re-acquiring slots between items.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Batch drain mode:** the audit runner can process multiple queued items (configurable N, default 5) in priority order within a single wall-clock budget (default 30 minutes). Items are dequeued, audited, slot released, next item dequeued.

2. **Priority order preserved:** items are drained from the queue in strict priority + FIFO order.

3. **Wall-clock budget enforced:** the batch drain stops after the configured time budget (default 30min) or when the queue is empty, whichever comes first. Remaining items stay queued for the next window.

4. **Slot release between items:** after each audit completes (success or failure), the concurrency slot is released so other processes can use it before the next item is dequeued.

5. **Observability — batch metrics:** each batch run logs: batch_start=<ts>, batch_end=<ts>, items_processed=<N>, queue_remaining=<N>, items_included=[id1, id2, ...].

6. **Integration tests:** batch drain behavior tested under saturation — verify multiple items drain per window vs. one-at-a-time.

## Implementation

- **File:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — add a batch drain loop that calls `_acquire_audit_slot()` in a queue-aware manner for multiple items
- **Config:** `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS=5` env var (default 5), `AUDIT_BATCH_TIMEOUT=1800` env var (default 30min)
- **Trigger:** batch mode activated when queue has >= 2 items; otherwise process single-item (backward compatible)

## Dependencies

- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (shared priority queue module)
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (audit runner queue integration)

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — new batch drain logic
- `skill/shared/queue.py` — priority queue (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` — integration tests (new)

## Goal

Extend the test skill's subprocess launch mechanism (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) to use the shared semaphore/queue primitive for bounded concurrency, preventing test runs from colliding with in-flight audits (which auto-execute tests via F3).

## Problem

The audit skill's F3 auto-execution runs the test skill (`run_tests.py`) when needed. Test runs consume CPU and can collide with concurrent audits for host resources. While the test cache dedupes most runs, unbounded test concurrency means an audit-triggered test run can starve the audit or vice versa.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Bounded test concurrency:** `run_tests.py` uses the shared semaphore (from `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) to bound concurrent test runs, just as the audit runner bounds concurrent audits.

2. **Separate semaphore namespace:** test runs use a "test" semaphore name (not "audit") so the two workloads are independently bounded. The shared queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L) can be extended to support multiple named semaphores.

3. **Configurable via env:** test concurrency cap controlled via `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (audit default) vs. `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (test default) env vars.

4. **No regression to cache behavior:** test cache read/write, per-repo dedup, and TTL behavior are unchanged.

5. **Integration test:** `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` verifies concurrent test runs are bounded by the semaphore.

## Implementation

- **File:** `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — add semaphore acquire/release around test execution
- **Config:** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env var, default 2
- **Optional:** extend `skill/shared/queue.py` to support a second named semaphore (test)

## Dependencies

- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (shared priority queue module)

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/queue.py` — shared queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L)

## Goal

Collect data and make a recommendation on whether the herdr downtime dispatcher's strict idle gate for audit dispatch should be relaxed. This is a research/investigation item — it produces a recommendation, not code changes (unless the recommendation is to change the gate).

## Problem

The herdr idle gate requires >= 60s continuous idle + >= 2 free slots before dispatching ANY work (including audits). This gate is the hard throughput ceiling: even with a bounded queue and batch drain, audits can only run when this gate opens. We need data to decide if relaxing this gate for audit-only dispatch is necessary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Data collection:** after deploying SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM + SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (bounded queue + batch drain), collect 7-day metrics on:
   - Gate opening frequency (how many windows per day)
   - Average window duration
   - Items drained per window (with batch drain)
   - Resulting time-to-audit for items in various priority tiers

2. **Analysis:** compute the theoretical throughput under current gate vs. proposed relaxed gate options:
   - Current: gate opens every ~X minutes, N items drained per window
   - Relaxed gate (audit-only, 10s idle OR any idle when slots available): estimated openings per day, throughput

3. **Recommendation with evidence:** a documented recommendation (keep gate / relax for audits / remove gate) with supporting metrics from step 1-2.

4. **Actionable next step:** if recommendation is to change the gate, create a child work item in the herdr ContextHub worklog (or here if in SorraAgents repo scope) with a clear implementation plan.

## Output

- Comment on this work item with the analysis and recommendation
- If gate change is recommended: create a follow-up work item with implementation plan

## Dependencies

- None (can be done in parallel with implementation of SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L / SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM)

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — idle gate logic (ContextHub)
- Audit queue metrics logs — from SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM + SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 deployment

# Audit Staleness Race: Post-Persist Comment Bumps updatedAt Past auditedAt

## Headline Summary

A race condition causes passed audits to display a stale icon (⏳) when a comment is added after `wl audit-set`, because the `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` call bumps `updatedAt` past the 60-second freshness window relative to `auditedAt`.

## Problem Statement

When `wl audit-set` persists a passed audit, it sets `auditedAt` to the current time. If any subsequent command (e.g., `wl comment add`) calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()`, the `updatedAt` timestamp advances. The `isAuditFresh()` check in `icons.ts` compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60000` ms — so a comment added more than 60s after the audit makes `isAuditFresh` return `false`, causing the TUI and selection lists to show a stale icon (⏳) instead of the ready icon (✅).

## Users / User Stories

- **Developer using `wl audit`**: After passing an audit and seeing ✅, a subsequent comment should not invalidate the audit result display.
- **Operator reviewing work items**: The selection list and TUI should accurately reflect audit freshness, not be confused by post-audit comments.
- **Automated agents (pi)**: Agent comments added as part of audit-close workflows should not cause false stale indications.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: Persisting a passed audit then immediately adding the audit-result comment does NOT make `isAuditFresh` return false — passed audits retain the ✅ icon in selection lists and the stage display icon past the 60s buffer.
- **AC2**: Skill/docs contract updated — `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and/or `skill/implement/SKILL.md` explicitly orders `wl comment add` **before** `persist_audit.py` / `wl audit-set`, or states that the audit report itself is the record and no separate post-persist comment is needed.
- **AC3**: Fix preserves existing guarantees — `needsProducerReview`-only flips still preserve `updatedAt`, content-fingerprint freshness still works, and normal (non-audit) comments still bump `updatedAt`.
- **AC4**: Regression test coverage — test that `wl audit-set` followed by `wl comment add` within the audit flow does not regress to stale display, or that the runner/list helper correctly reports fresh when comment precedes audit.

## Constraints

- No behavior change for non-audit comments — they must still bump `updatedAt`.
- Do not regress runner re-audit / child-audit freshness logic.
- The 60s staleness buffer for non-audit contexts is unchanged.
- Content-fingerprint freshness (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) must continue to work.

## Implementation

The root cause was that `persist_audit.py` fetched the work-item stage and passed `--stage` to `wl update --audit-text`, causing `db.update()` to bump `updatedAt`. The fix removes the stage-fetch + `--stage` injection from `_run_audit_text_update()` in `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`. Stage/status transitions are handled by the audit runner's `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`.

- Commit: `6cf97001` (fix: remove --stage from persist_audit audit-text update)
- Merge commit: `285d03dd` (merged into dev)

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `createComment() → touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` (line 3369), `update()` metadata vs content bump (line 1299)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` (line 310), `stageDisplayIcon()` (line 333)
- `packages/shared/src/theme.ts` — mirror of icon logic
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — `persist_audit()` function (FIXED)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — freshness gates (`_check_audit_freshness`)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` / `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — persistence and close ordering docs

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD** — ContextHub Leader lease zombie fix (observed failure example: auditedAt 13:49:12, updatedAt 13:51:09, comment delta 117s)
- **WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R** — needsProducerReview must not invalidate audit (precedent for preserve-updatedAt)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** — Content fingerprint / persist-write tolerance
- **SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4** — audit_runner parent flow loops re-triggering child audits
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** — Eliminate wasteful re-audits

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Changing `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` behavior for audit comments may affect downstream consumers that rely on `updatedAt` tracking. **Mitigation**: Scope change narrowly to audit-result comments only.
- **Risk**: Option B (atomic bundle) requires schema change to `rawOutput`/`auditText` handling. **Mitigation**: Option A (fix persist_audit.py) was implemented instead.
- **Assumption**: The 60s buffer is intentional for non-audit contexts and should not be removed or significantly altered.
- **Assumption**: Content-fingerprint freshness is the preferred long-term solution; this fix addresses the immediate TUI/list display issue.
- **Scope**: This fix addresses the parent-item comment ordering issue only. Child-audit non-cascade (all 6 children showed 🔍) is a separate issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- N/A — The work item description is sufficiently detailed. No clarifying questions needed.

## Summary

`audit_runner.py issue|batch --do-not-persist` currently skips **all** persistence, including the `auditedAt` timestamp. A successful dry-run validation (`Ready to close: Yes`) therefore leaves `auditedAt` stale. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:250`) stays `false`, so Herdr's selection list / DOWNTIME audit tier correctly re-queues the item as a stale-audit candidate and shows the ⏳ stale-passed state.

Observed on 2026-09-01 with `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV`: validated with `--do-not-persist --force` (`Ready to close: Yes`, deep analysis completed) but stored audit remained `2026-08-11T05:13:22Z` while `updatedAt` had advanced to `2026-09-01T18:33:14Z` (delta ~21 days via `herdr-downtime` claim + comments). Herdr was correct to show "out of date" — the dry-run never refreshed the freshness signal. Manual `wl audit-set` was required to make `updatedAt == auditedAt` and restore `isAuditFresh: true`.

## Problem

- `--do-not-persist` is documented as a dry run but gives no freshness guarantee; operators assume a passing validation will clear the stale flag, but it does not.
- Help text (`audit_runner.py:10656`, `10781` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) says only "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" — does not explain the Herdr staleness consequence nor the intended dry-run semantics.

## User story

As an operator running `audit_runner.py --do-not-persist` for a dry-run validation, I want a passing validation to still refresh the audit freshness timestamp so Herdr no longer shows the item as out of date, while the full raw report remains not persisted; the flag's help should make this contract explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Freshness on dry-run success:** When `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` (and `batch --do-not-persist` for each drained item) completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item's `auditedAt` is atomically updated to `now` (`updatedAt == auditedAt` in the same txn, `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` pattern) with `auditResult`/`readyToClose` reflecting the verdict, **without** persisting the full `rawOutput` markdown. `isAuditFresh` must be `true` immediately after, and `wl list --stage in_review --json` must show `auditedAt == updatedAt` and `isAuditFresh: true` (Herdr shows ✅ not ⏳ and excludes from audit tier). When the verdict is `Ready to close: No` / `partial` / failure, `auditedAt` is **not** bumped (fail-closed — a failed dry-run must not clear staleness).
2. **Help text updated:** `--do-not-persist` help on both `issue` and `batch` subparsers (and the `SKILL.md` flag table / persistence procedure) is updated to state: dry-run — full audit report is not stored, but on `Ready to close: Yes` the audit freshness timestamp (`auditedAt`/`auditResult`) is still persisted so Herdr/DOWNTIME treat the item as freshly audited; omit the flag to persist the full report. The previous terse "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" is replaced.
3. **No regression for full persist:** Without the flag, behavior is unchanged — full report + `auditedAt`/`auditResult` persisted atomically and lifecycle transitions (`completed`/`in_review` etc.) still apply. With the flag, lifecycle transitions still apply (flag does not suppress status/stage changes).
4. **Tests:** Unit/cli tests cover the new contract: (a) `--do-not-persist` + `Yes` bumps `auditedAt`/`auditResult` but leaves `rawOutput` empty/absent; (b) `--do-not-persist` + `No` does not bump; (c) help text contains the freshness/dry-run wording (mirrors `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` pattern for SKILL.md validation).
5. **Docs:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` persistence section and runner flag docs updated to match the new flag semantics.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` (dry-run left Herdr stale, required manual `wl audit-set` to recover).
- Implementation hint: reuse the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes|no` path (sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in one txn) for the dry-run success case, passing summary but omitting `--raw-output`/`--audit-file` so `rawOutput` stays null. Do not call `wl update --audit-text` afterwards (that would bump `updatedAt` past `auditedAt + 60s` and re-stale).
- `batch` subcommand should apply the same rule per-item in the drain loop.
- Consider whether a new flag (e.g. `--truly-do-not-persist`) is needed for the rare case where even freshness must not be touched; default should be the freshness-preserving dry-run.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` — effort-and-risk SKILL.md output path (the stale-audit observation)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:isAuditFresh` — `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:selectAuditCandidate` / `isAuditFresh` — audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10656,10781` — flag definition
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py:495` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` note


## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `--do-not-persist` flag definition and persistence logic
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` transaction logic
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` function
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate()` / `isAuditFresh` audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — runner documentation, flag table, persistence procedure
- `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` — SKILL.md validation test pattern

# Test skill `--type` parameter (smoke/unit/full) with local CWD extension

**Headline:** Add a `--type smoke|unit|full` selector to the test skill so projects can run fast, locally-defined test profiles during implementation while preserving the full-suite cache/evidence contract at release and audit gates.

**Parent:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (Local skill extensions for global skills) — this item **depends on / is blocked by** the parent until its CWD extension convention lands.

## Problem

The global `test` skill currently only runs the **full** test suite. There is no typed entry point to select a lighter test type during implementation or audit without paying the full ~15-minute suite cost. Projects such as Tableau Card Engine already define fast profiles in their own `AGENTS.md` (unit ~seconds, smoke ~2m, dev ~3.5m, full ~15m), but the skill has no way to invoke them and no convention for a project to declare them locally.

A parallel effort, SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 ("Local skill extensions for global skills"), will allow any global skill to be extended by the invoking project via a CWD convention. The test skill must consume that extension mechanism so per-project test strategies are defined **locally in the consuming repo**, never hardcoded in SorraAgents.

## Users

- **Producer / agent running `/skill:test`** — wants `unit` during implementation (seconds of feedback) and `full` only at release/audit gates, without editing the global skill.
- **Project maintainer** — wants to declare project-specific test commands per type in their own repo (cwd), and to add new types beyond the minimum set.

Example user stories:

- *As an implementing agent,* I run `/skill:test --type unit` in a worktree and get feedback in seconds, instead of waiting ~15 minutes for the full suite.
- *As a project maintainer,* I add a `dev` and `e2e` type to my local extension and they work without any change to the global skill.
- *As a release agent,* I run `/skill:test --type full` (or bare `/skill:test`) and get the auditable full-suite contract unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CLI parameter and validation.** `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (and therefore the `/skill:test` entry point) accepts `--type <value>`. The minimum accepted values are `smoke`, `unit`, and `full`. `full` is the default when `--type` is omitted. An unknown value exits non-zero with a clear error that lists the currently allowed values (the minimum set plus any locally-defined types). `--help` documents the parameter.
2. **Machine-readable local CWD extension delegation.** When a local test-skill extension is present in the invoking project (discovered under the CWD convention provided by SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0), the runner resolves the requested type's command(s) from it. The mapping MUST be machine-readable by the runner (prose-only guidance is insufficient). When the extension exists but omits the requested minimum type, the runner fails with a clear diagnostic naming the missing type and the extension file — it must NOT silently substitute the full suite.
3. **Local extensions may define additional types.** A local extension may define extra types beyond the minimum (e.g. `dev`, `e2e`, `quick`) and additional strategies. The global skill accepts and dispatches any locally-defined type, not just the three minimum values; the error message for an unknown type lists locally-defined types too.
4. **Fallback when no local extension exists.** When no local extension is found, the runner falls back to existing convention detection for the minimum types: `full` → `full_suite_commands(project_root)` (unchanged); `unit` → the convention-detected unit subset (e.g. pytest `tests/unit`, node `tests/unit/**/*.mjs`) when one exists. When no convention subset can be resolved for the requested type, the runner exits with a clear diagnostic — it must NOT silently run the full suite.
5. **Existing behaviour preserved (backwards compatibility).** A bare invocation with no `--type` remains `full` and preserves the existing full-suite contract: caching (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W / SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY), scope handling (SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC), `.pi/test-config.json` override, triage flow, and audit-skill cache consumption. `--json` and `--summary` usage is not regressed.
6. **`--type` and `--scope` are orthogonal; typed runs are never full-suite evidence.** `--type` selects the command profile; `--scope full|changed` continues to select full-vs-changed within that profile. Only a `--type full` run populates the full-suite cache entry the audit skill accepts; non-`full` typed runs use independent cache keys and record their type in the result JSON/metadata so a partial run can never satisfy a "full test suite passes" AC. `--summary` output reflects the recorded type.
7. **Tests.** New behaviour is covered by tests (type parsing/defaults, local-extension delegation, additional locally-defined types, unknown-type errors, incomplete local maps, fallback conventions, and backwards compatibility).
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `skill/test/SKILL.md` (typed invocation, minimum types, local extension contract, implementation-vs-release guidance), and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The local extension file location and format must follow the convention introduced by SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0; this item must not invent a separate discovery path. If that convention is prose-only (`SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md` guidance), this item must contribute the machine-readable mapping under the same convention (e.g. a JSON file inside the same `.pi/skills_extensions/test/` directory) rather than a new discovery mechanism.
- The global skill must not hardcode project-specific commands (e.g. Tableau Card Engine vitest profiles). Project specifics belong in the local extension, discoverable at cwd.
- Backwards compatible: existing callers with no `--type` flag see no behaviour change.
- The skill remains usable from any cwd, including when invoked with `--worklog-dir` / prefix-to-sibling resolution; the runner resolves the invoking project via `detect_project_root()`.
- UK English spelling in docs and help text.

## Existing state

- Runner: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — resolves `full_suite_commands(project_root)` from `.pi/test-config.json` or conventions (npm-test / pytest / node dirs). Existing selectors: `--suite pytest|node|all` and `--scope full|changed`. No `--type` entry point. `detect_project_root()` already resolves the invoking project root.
- Docs: `skill/test/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` document the full-suite workflow, cache contract, and scope behaviour.
- Parent: SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (in_progress, stage `idea`) proposes `.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/SKILL_PREFIX.md` and `SKILL_POSTFIX.md` — currently **prose guidance only**. No machine-readable extension loader exists on disk yet, so the exact extension file format is unresolved (see Risks & assumptions and Open Questions).

## Desired change

1. **Parent first:** land SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 so CWD extension discovery (and a machine-readable mapping format) is available.
2. **Then this item:** add `--type` to `run_tests.py` and `SKILL.md`, wire delegation to the local CWD extension when present, implement the convention fallbacks, emit clear errors for unknown/missing types, keep `--scope`/cache/evidence semantics correct, and add tests + docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — add `--type` (default `full`); type→command resolution (local extension first, convention fallback); type-aware cache keys/evidence metadata; clear unknown/incomplete-type diagnostics.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — document `--type`, the minimum types, the local extension contract, and implementation-vs-release guidance.

- Local extension file (path per SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0, likely under `.pi/skills_extensions/test/`) — the project-provided type→command map consumed by the runner.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 will expose (or will be extended by this item to expose) a stable, machine-readable CWD extension mapping. If the parent's convention changes, this item must follow it. *Mitigation:* this item contributes the machine-readable mapping under the parent's path rather than inventing a new one.
- **Risk:** the parent's current proposal is prose-only (`SKILL_PREFIX.md`/`SKILL_POSTFIX.md`), which a script cannot reliably parse. *Mitigation:* require a machine-readable mapping (e.g. `.pi/skills_extensions/test/test-config.json` or a `types` map in `.pi/test-config.json`) and record the interface in the parent.
- **Risk:** a local extension defines an incomplete type map (e.g. missing `unit`). *Mitigation:* fail with a clear diagnostic (AC2), never silently run full.
- **Risk:** type-specific runs pollute the full-suite cache and get mistaken for full-suite evidence by the audit skill. *Mitigation:* independent cache keys + recorded `type`, audit rejects non-`full` (AC6).
- **Risk (scope creep):** pressure to add many new types or a generic "test strategy DSL". *Mitigation:* the minimum set is fixed here; extra types are the project's responsibility via the local extension. Additional opportunities are recorded as separate work items rather than folded into this one.
- **Risk:** dangling work-item references in the original brief (`SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC`, `SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61`) do not resolve in the SA worklog (verified via `wl show`/data grep); they are retained here only as historical context. The behaviour they describe is documented in `skill/test/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0** — Local skill extensions for global skills (parent, blocking). Provides the CWD extension mechanism.
- **SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W** — Audit: execute test suite read-only to verify full-suite ACs automatically (completed). Defines the cache/evidence contract preserved by AC5/AC6.

- **SA-0MTP1IM5N008JYLN** — Scope audit code-quality gate to item's changed files (open). Related scope/caching concern.
- **SA-0MSJELL44009XYIL**, **SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD** — node suite-dir/glob resolution conventions that AC4's fallback must respect.
- **CG-0MT5XO7DI0066QCT** — Tableau Card Engine audit that motivated this item (full-suite auto-execute timeout).

## Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH** – Remove skill/ralph/ directory tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08K8009WH9A** – Remove workflow-descriptor validators (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive clarifying questions were required: the seed context (authored brief) was sufficient to draft the problem, users, ACs, and constraints. Two design points could not be resolved from repo search and are recorded below as OPEN QUESTIONS with the research behind them.

- **Q: What machine-readable format should the type→command map use?** — **OPEN QUESTION.** Research: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` already defines `.pi/test-config.json` (`suiteCommands`, `timeoutPerCommand`) as the machine-readable extension precedent (AC6 of the seed). The parent SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 currently proposes only prose files (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`); grep across the repo and `git log --all` found no extension loader on disk. Proposed resolution (documented assumption, to be confirmed when the parent lands): the child contributes a machine-readable mapping under the parent's convention (e.g. `.pi/skills_extensions/test/test-config.json`) or extends `.pi/test-config.json` with a `types` map, without introducing a new discovery path.
- **Q: How do `--type` and the existing `--scope full|changed` interact, and may a non-`full` type satisfy a full-suite AC?** — **ANSWER (by analogy to existing contract, recorded as a constraint).** Research: `--scope changed` runs already use independent cache keys and are rejected by the audit's full-suite query; `--scope` is documented in `skill/test/SKILL.md` (`SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC`). This brief requires `--type` to be orthogonal to `--scope`, and only `--type full` to populate the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry (AC6).

This refines the seed's "fallback to sensible defaults" wording: convention fallback where a convention exists, clear diagnostic otherwise.
- **Q: Do the referenced work items `SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC` and `SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61` exist?** — **ANSWER: No.** Research: `wl show` returns "Work item not found" and a direct grep of `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` finds no matches; the ids remain in `skill/test/SKILL.md` / `skill/audit/SKILL.md` as historical references. Recorded as stale references; the behaviour they describe is documented in the skill docs. (A separate low-priority cleanup item may be warranted; not in scope here.)

While this is an expected pattern for epics (implicit success = all children resolved), the audit tool requires explicit ACs to verify and produce a "met" verdict.

Goal: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria on the epic that reflect its actual purpose:
- Epic tracks all code quality findings discovered during automated code review
- Epic is satisfied when all child work items are resolved
- New findings discovered after closure warrant a new epic

Proposed ACs:
1. All code quality findings discovered during audit are tracked as child work items
2. All child work items are resolved (completed) before epic can close
3. New code quality findings discovered after epic closure are captured in a new epic

This will allow the audit tool to produce "Ready to close: Yes" when all children are resolved.

# Intake Brief — Session isolation per child when implementing an epic

**Work item:** SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 — "When implementing an epic start a new session for each child"
**Priority:** high | **Type:** epic

## Problem statement

When implementing an epic, all children are currently implemented within a single LLM session. Each child inherits the accumulated context of all previous children, diluting focus and risking context contamination between unrelated tasks.

## Users

- **AI agents** — multi-child epic implementations that currently run serially in one session.
- **Producers/operators** — agents that dispatch work via `/skill:implement` on parent items.

Example user story: "As an AI agent implementing epic SA-XXXX, when I invoke `/skill:implement SA-XXXX`, each child should be implemented in its own LLM session, giving it a clean context window focused solely on that child's ACs."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New session per child.** When implementing an epic, a new LLM session is started for each child item — each child receives a clean context window containing only that child's work-item description, ACs, and relevant context.
2. **Serial execution preserved.** Children are still implemented in dependency order (blocking items first), but each in its own session — the serial ordering remains intact.
3. **Session logging.** Each new session comments on the child work-item with its session ID: `<agent_action> - Session ID: <pi_session_id> - <path_to_sessions_log>` (per existing AGENTS.md convention).
4. **Parent still advanced last.** The parent item is only advanced to `in_review` after all children (across all sessions) have reached terminal status.
5. **Error isolation.** A failure in one child's session does not affect subsequent children's sessions; the parent phase reports which children failed and which succeeded.

## Constraints

- This is a procedural/organizational change — no code changes to the implement skill itself (which already handles parent recursion).
- The change applies to both AI agents and human operators following the workflow.
- Session boundaries must be explicit: each child's session starts with a fresh context, re-loading the work-item description and ACs.
- Worktree isolation per child is already in place and must be preserved.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 (Parent recursion): children are implemented serially within the same session ("Then implement that child by recursing into this procedure... and re-run `implement.py parent <parent-id>` for the next child").
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` workflow step 8: "End session — inform operator, summarize remaining tasks, clean up worktrees." — currently applied once at the end of the entire epic, not per child.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` step 58: session logging convention exists but is applied per work-item on new Pi session start, not per-child.

## Desired change

Update the procedural guidance in `AGENTS.md` (both global and project-level) to specify:

1. When `/skill:implement <parent-id>` is invoked and the item has children, a **new Pi session should be started for each child**.
2. Each child's session begins with the child work-item's description, ACs, and context loaded fresh.
3. After completing a child, the session ends (per existing convention), worktrees are cleaned up, and the next child starts a new session.
4. The parent is only considered complete after all child sessions have finished.

## Key files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` — global agent guidance; add session-per-child procedural step
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` — project-level agent guidance; mirror the global change
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 — clarify that each child recursion implies a new session (documentation alignment)

## Related work

- SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T: "implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain" — the parent recursion mechanism that this epic builds on.
- SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR: "Reduce initial LLM context from skills and skill-related startup files" — related to context management but different scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — operational overhead:** starting new sessions per child means more session management. Mitigation: this is already the pattern for independent tasks; the overhead is minimal (session startup is fast).
- **Risk — context fragmentation:** each session must re-load relevant context for the child. Mitigation: the implement skill already loads the work-item description at session start.
- **Assumption:** "session" = Pi conversation session (with its own LLM context window); not a separate process or script.
- **Assumption:** serial execution is intentional and performance is not the primary concern; correctness and context isolation are.
- **Risk — scope creep:** this could evolve into a feature request for the implement skill itself to manage sessions. Mitigation: keep this epic scoped to procedural documentation; session orchestration is a separate concern.

# Integration Tests for Plan/Intake Tree Iteration & Coverage

## Problem statement

The audit of SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM found that while the shared helper functions (tree_coverage.py) and SKILL.md workflows are well-tested at the unit level, three acceptance criteria (AC1, AC2, AC4) lack end-to-end integration tests that exercise the actual skill mutation behavior:

- **AC1:** No integration test exercises the full plan skill workflow with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting end-to-end processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2:** No integration test exercises the full intake skill workflow with per-child intake runs and coverage verification.
- **AC4:** No test exercises the actual skill mutation behavior — adding missing child ACs, setting status=open with conflict comments, and blocking stage advancement on unresolvable conflicts.

## Users

- **Agents** running `/skill:plan` on epics with children — need confidence that the tree iteration processes correctly in a multi-level dependency graph.
- **Agents** running `/skill:intake` on decomposed epics — need confidence that per-child intake and coverage verification work as documented.
- **Operators** — need integration test coverage that validates the full workflow, not just the helper functions in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (plan integration):** A test creates a multi-level tree via `wl` commands (parent → 2 children, one child has a grandchild), sets up dependency edges, and runs the plan skill's tree-iteration step (or an equivalent agent-workflow script). The test asserts: every node is processed, the processing order respects `wl dep` edges (topological order with listed-order tie-breaking), and the final stage advancement comment is written.
- **AC2 (intake integration):** A test creates a parent with existing children that have partial AC coverage, runs the intake skill's per-child intake step, and asserts that: each child is processed, coverage is computed across children, and the coverage verification step either auto-closes gaps (when unambiguous) or stops (when conflicts exist).
- **AC3 (mutation behavior — auto-close):** A test simulates an unambiguous coverage gap (parent AC not covered by any child AC, but a clear mapping exists) and asserts that the skill workflow creates/updates a child work item to cover the gap, then advances to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC4 (mutation behavior — stop on conflict):** A test simulates an unresolvable conflict (parent AC cannot be mapped to any child AC, or mapping would invent requirements) and asserts that: the skill leaves the item in `open` status, writes a comment describing the conflict, and does NOT advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC5 (idempotence):** Re-running the integration test (with the same tree state) does not create duplicate children or duplicate comments, and the final state is identical to the first run.

## Constraints

- Tests must use the Worklog API only (`wl` CLI) — no direct file edits.
- Tests must work against the same worklog backend used in the existing test suite.
- Tests should create and clean up their own work items (ephemeral test tree).
- Must not modify or depend on audit, implement, or other skills' behavior.
- Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — Extend with integration-level tree workflow tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_plan_integration.py` / `skill/shared/tests/test_intake_integration.py` if a separate file is preferred).
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected processing order and mutation behavior.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected per-child intake and coverage verification.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM — Plan/intake skills: iterate over children, ensure child ACs collectively cover parent ACs (in_review).
- SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E — Audit runner circular dependency fix; reference for tree semantics.

# Intake Brief — Add Total Tokens breakdown to usage report before fallback frequency table (SA-0MTM3LKP1003S28J)

## Problem statement
The proxy usage report (`report.md`) jumps from session/request counts to fallback frequency without showing token volume. Operators need a Total Tokens (input + output) overview immediately before the fallback table to correlate cost/usage with why traffic fell back.

## Users
- **Proxy operators / SREs** — need token volume by time bucket (fast/cheap) and by model to reason about cost and capacity.
- **Capacity planners** — use fast/cheap split and per-model share to justify slot/context changes.

User stories:
- As an operator, I open the daily report and see a Total Tokens section before fallback reasons, so I know absolute and % share per bucket and per model without manual aggregation.
- As an operator, I can compare input vs output vs total tokens and their % share across fast/cheap and across models.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `report.md` contains a new section (e.g. `## Total tokens`) rendered **immediately before** `## Fallback reasons` (the fallback frequency table), in every run including zero-traffic windows (shows `0` or `-` with note).
- [ ] Table shows **Total Tokens = prompt (input) + completion (output)** summed from authoritative `tokens=prompt/completion/total` on `Stream finished` lines (never payload truncation); displays Input, Output, and Total as absolute counts and % share where applicable, with consistent formatting/rounding.
- [ ] **Fast/cheap breakdown**: for the same token totals, shows absolute token counts and % of total for the fast bucket and cheap bucket (bucketing follows existing mode-aware fast/cheap logic — mode timeline / slot schedule keyed by session start; unattributed streams excluded or documented).
- [ ] **By-model breakdown**: shows absolute token counts and % of total grouped by provider/model (same grouping as existing per-model breakdown), with absolute + % columns and sorted by total desc (or documented order); handles unknown provider/model as documented placeholder and empty-model case.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Source of truth for sizes is `tokens=prompt/completion/total` on `Stream finished` lines aggregated in `aggregation.py`; do not use truncated payload sizes.
- Reuse existing bucketing (`bucketing.py` / `ModeScheduleMap` + `SlotSchedule`) so fast/cheap shares match the report's other tables; zero-division and empty-window cases must not error.
- Output location/format must not break archival or `report.md` consumers; keep change surgical to `reporting.py` + aggregation if needed.
- Implementation lives in `llm-manager` skill `proxy-usage-analysis` but this work item is tracked in `SorraAgents` — cross-repo delivery; tests in `llm-manager/.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`.

## Existing state
- Skill: `proxy-usage-analysis` in `llm-manager` (`/.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`). Report built in `scripts/reporting.py:build_report()` — currently goes Session summary → `## Fallback reasons` → error/routing-skip → per-model breakdown → TTC/speed/busy. No token-volume section exists.
- Token data is parsed in `log_parser.py` (`RE_TOKENS`, `prompt/completion/total`) and aggregated per-session in `aggregation.py` (`SessionStats.start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `avg_response_size`, `max_response_size`, `builder.local_completion`). Global token sums per bucket/model are not yet exposed.
- Work item `SA-0MTM3LKP1003S28J` (feature, medium, `idea`→`in_progress` assignee Map) seeded from the request.

## Desired change
- Extend aggregation (if needed) to expose summed prompt/completion/total tokens and per-bucket / per-model token totals.
- In `reporting.py`, insert a new `## Total tokens` section immediately before `## Fallback reasons`, rendering a table (or compact pair of tables) covering: Total (Input / Output / Total) and breakdowns by fast/cheap (absolute + %) and by model (absolute + %).
- Update `SKILL.md` Outputs/limitations and any report-interpretation docs; add/extend unit + e2e tests with fixtures covering fast/cheap and multi-model token mixes, and empty-window case.
- Verify with `/skill:test` in `llm-manager`.

## Key Files
- `proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Add new Total Tokens section before fallback reasons; add helper to format absolute + % columns.
- `proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Expose summed token totals per session/window, per bucket, per model if not already available.
- `proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — Reference for `tokens=` regex; no change expected.
- `proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — Document new report section in Outputs.
- `proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` + `tests/fixtures.py` — Add coverage for new section, fast/cheap and model token breakdown.

## Related work
- Potentially related docs: `llm-manager/.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `scripts/reporting.py`, `scripts/aggregation.py`.
- Potentially related work items: no direct proxy-usage duplicates found via `wl search` in either worklog; related runtime context LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation) cited in report Notes.

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: double-counting or mismatched definition of Total (prompt+completion vs `total` field) — mitigation: define Total = prompt + completion summed from `tokens=` and document; add test asserting invariant.
- Risk: bucket attribution drift (mode-aware vs legacy schedule) — mitigation: reuse existing `profile`/`_bucket_profile` logic and mode_map path.
- Risk: large-window perf if summing per-event — negligible vs streaming already in place.
- Assumption: every `Stream finished` with `tokens=` is authoritative; lines without tokens contribute 0 and are noted.
- Assumption: feature — net-new capability (not a bug fix for incorrect current behavior).
- Scope-creep mitigation: extra token visualizations (charts, per-hour tokens) recorded as separate linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Which token fields define Total Tokens — `total` from the log line or prompt+completion?" — Answer (assumed, to confirm in review): Total = prompt (input) + completion (output) from `tokens=prompt/completion/total` on `Stream finished`; input = sum(prompt), output = sum(completion), total = input+output. Source: inferred from request "Total Tokens (input and output)" plus `log_parser.py` authoritative tokens; open to producer confirmation.
- Q: "Do fast/cheap percentages share the grand total, and does model breakdown cover the same grand total?" — Answer (assumed): Yes — both breakdowns are shares of the same grand Total Tokens, so fast%+cheap% = 100% and model %s sum to 100%. Cross-check in review.
- Q: "Where exactly is 'before the table covering fallback frequency'?" — Answer (assumed): Immediately before `## Fallback reasons` in `reporting.py:build_report()` (≈ line 343). Source: repo inspection.

Notes on idempotence: Re-running this intake should update the description rather than duplicating entries; Q/A above are assumed pending producer confirmation.

# One last validation before final ship

## Problem statement

The ship skill's release gating has five checks (unmerged branches, audit readiness, critical items, worklog refs, producer review) — but none of them perform a comprehensive sweep of all completed/in_review items for audit health. Items with stale, missing, or failing audits — or those flagged for producer review — can slip through because the existing audit gate only covers top-level items and the producer-review gate has its own scoping. This creates a risk that items with audit problems reach the release undetected.

## Users

- **Agent (Map):** Needs a reliable final gate that catches all audit and producer-review gaps before dev→main merge.
- **Producer:** Needs visibility into items that genuinely require review attention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new gating step (Step 3.7) is added to `run-release.js` that scans **all** `in_review` items (both top-level and child items) for:
   a. Missing audits (no audit record exists)
   b. Stale audits (audit exists but is outdated)
   c. Failing audits (audit reports not ready to close, not transient)
   d. Producer-review flags (`needsProducerReview = true`)
2. For missing or stale audits: the gate auto-remediates by re-running the audit runner (`audit_runner.py issue <id>`), then re-checks; items that pass after remediation are unblocked; items that still fail are reported as blocking.
3. For failing audits: items are reported as blocking immediately (no re-audit attempt for genuine "not ready to close" verdicts).
4. For items flagged for producer review: they are reported as blocking with remediation guidance.
5. The gate produces a clear, actionable report listing all blocking items with reasons and remediation commands, and exits with a dedicated exit code (e.g., 12) when blocking items are found.
6. A new script `check-final-validation.js` is created in `skill/ship/scripts/` following the existing pattern, with injectable command boundaries for test isolation.
7. All existing tests pass; new unit tests cover the gating logic with injected command boundaries.

## Constraints

- Must follow the existing ship skill check pattern (check-*.js files, injectable boundaries).
- Must not break existing gate ordering or exit codes.
- Must be consistent with the audit gate's remediation strategy (re-run audit_runner, never direct `wl update`).
- `--skip-checks` bypasses this gate like all others.
- Scope: only add the new check — no other changes to the ship skill.

## Existing state

The ship skill has five gating steps in `run-release.js`:
1. Unmerged branches (exit 3)
2. Audit readiness (exit 6) — top-level `in_review` items only
3. Critical items (exit 7)
3.5. Worklog refs (exit 8)
3.6. Producer review (exit 9)

The audit gate (`check-audit-gate.js`) already handles missing/transient audit auto-remediation for top-level items only. Child items are excluded by design (covered by parent audits). The producer-review gate checks top-level items only.

## Desired change

Add a sixth gate (Step 3.7) that:
- Queries **all** `in_review` items (no parentId filter — includes children)
- Checks each item's audit status (missing, stale, failing, or producer-review flagged)
- Auto-remediates missing/stale audits via re-run
- Reports all blocking items with actionable remediation
- Uses a new exit code (12) for this gate

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Add Step 3.7 gating call
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — New check script (create)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — May need a shared `getAuditStatus()` or `attemptAuditRemediation()` export for reuse
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.test.js` — Add tests for the new gate
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — Document new gate and exit code 12

## Related work

- SA-0MS4TJR2R0043UHO: Extend getCandidateItems and add checkProducerReviewStatus (producer-review gate foundation)
- SA-0MSUT8GQP004WSYN: Audit gate conservative remediation pattern (reference for auto-remediation)
- SA-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR: Code Freeze marker contract (gating infrastructure reference)
- SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB: Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill (original audit gate)

# Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: phases `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` and `_phase_fetch_and_cq` fail to use commit references stored only in comments, and treat arbitrary hex found in prose as cherry-pick candidates, producing a spurious merge-gate blocker and a false-negative audit.

Discovered during audit of OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm, `--force` run, work already present in `origin/dev`).

## Symptom

- Work item has no feature branch and no commit in its description; its real implementation commit is referenced only in a comment (e.g. `235ef18` for OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S).
- Merge gate logs `integrating (branch=none, commits=[9b0f...])` then fails: `git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object` and blocks the audit.
- `9b0f500f...` is a *foreign* autiobook reference pinned in the description (reference, not a commit in the owning repo). `235ef18` (the real commit) is never discovered.

## Root cause

1. **Comments not fetched early for merge gate.** `_phase_fetch_and_cq` loads the top-level `comments` from `wl show` into a separate binding, but `ctx.work_item.get("comments", [])` (or the equivalent) is still the default empty list when the merge gate resolves evidence, so commit shas referenced only in comments are never seen. Reproduction: `wl show OSL-... --children --json` has `workItem.comments` absent while top-level `comments` holds the Map commit.

2. **Over-broad hex extraction.** `re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE)` picks up arbitrary hex strings (foreign repo refs, docs examples) and enqueues them as cherry-pick targets. The failing run treated `9b0f500f...` (from `9b0f500f11f...`, an autiobook pin) as a required candidate and failed closed when that object was absent.

3. **Interaction.** Because (1) left `commits=[foreign_hex]`, (2) caused the integration failure path; the item *was* already on `origin/dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`) but was rejected.

## Proposed fix

- Fetch and bind `comments` on `ctx` before `_phase_merge_gate` (or pass `comments` into `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`).
- Filter integration candidates to objects that actually exist or are already ancestors of `origin/dev` (e.g. `git cat-file -e <sha>` / `rev-parse --verify` check, or skip foreign shas that are not ancestors and not branch tips), so that documentation hex cited as reference does not force cherry-pick.
- Optionally, scope hex extraction to producer-attributed commit citations (e.g. `see commit <hex>`) rather than every hex token in prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A work item whose only commit citation is in a top-level comment (no branch, no 7+ hex in description) is correctly merged-gated: evidence resolves the commented commit and `containment` verifies it against `origin/dev`.
2. Hex tokens that are not objects in the owning repo (or are cited only as foreign-repo pinned references, not deliverable commits) do not cause `fatal: bad object` or a spurious merge-gate block.
3. Existing behaviour for feature-branch and description-referenced commits is preserved (regression tests).
4. No new behaviour breaks `wl show` clients: comment binding is done in the audit runner only.

## Evidence

- Failing run (`open_source_llm`, `235ef18` already in `origin/dev`):
  ```
  Merge gate: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S work NOT present in origin/dev — integrating (branch=none, commits=["9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b"])
  git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object
  ```
- Manual verification: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`.
- Stored blocker audit: `wl audit-show OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S --json` (open_source_llm).

## Related

- Proposer work item: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm). See its audit trail and producer-review comment id OSL-C0MTQA3R4E0084LBY.
- Worktree remains at `open_source_llm/.worklog/worktrees/audit-merge-OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S` (remove manually once triaged).
data.title: Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

# Audit Stuck in `in_progress` When `run-release` is Aborted

## Problem Statement

When the `run-release` script is aborted (e.g., via Ctrl+C or signal) while the audit gate is running audits on work items, those items are left stuck in the `in_progress` state. The audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` claim is performed before the try/finally block in `cmd_issue` can catch the abort, and a hard kill (SIGKILL) bypasses Python's finally blocks entirely. This breaks the release pipeline because items stuck in `in_progress` are excluded from the `in_review` candidate query.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Runs `run-release` and needs the pipeline to complete or abort cleanly without manual work-item intervention.
- **Automated agents**: Agents waiting for work items to reach `in_review` stage to proceed with release gating.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Audit runner restores pre-audit status on hard abort**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGKILL (signal 9) during an audit, it must still restore the work item to its pre-audit state (`completed`/`in_review` or whatever it was before the audit). This requires a signal handler that captures the original status and resets it on `SIGKILL` via `SIGSYS`/`prctl` or a wrapper mechanism — since Python cannot directly catch SIGKILL, the solution must use a subprocess wrapper or a separate watchdog process.
2. **AC2 — Audit runner restores status on SIGTERM/SIGINT**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the status restoration must still complete even if killed mid-try-block. Currently, the `finally` block in `cmd_issue` handles this, but it must be verified to always execute (e.g., via signal handlers that re-raise after cleanup).
3. **AC3 — No `in_progress` items left after any abort scenario**: After any termination of `audit_runner.py` (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL, or process death), the audited work item must NOT remain in `in_progress` state. This can be verified by checking the work item's status after a forced kill.
4. **AC4 — All existing audit tests pass**: The fix must not break any existing audit tests in `skill/audit/tests/`.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce new race conditions in concurrent audit scenarios (multiple `audit_runner.py` processes auditing the same or different items).
- The solution must follow existing project conventions: no direct `wl update` outside the audit runner's lifecycle management.
- If a direct Python-level SIGKILL handler is impossible, a wrapper mechanism (e.g., a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death) must be used.

## Existing State

- The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `in_progress` status in `_phase_gate` (line 7450) before entering the main `try/finally` block in `cmd_issue`.
- The `finally` block in `cmd_issue` calls `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` which restores the pre-audit state.
- `check-audit-gate.js` (used by `run-release.js`) invokes `audit_runner.py issue <id>` via `execSync` for each candidate work item.
- When the `run-release` script is aborted, the `execSync` call is terminated, killing the `audit_runner.py` child process.
- If killed with SIGKILL (signal 9), Python's `finally` blocks do not execute, leaving the item in `in_progress`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Needs a signal handling mechanism or wrapper to ensure status restoration on hard abort.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — May need a timeout/abort handler to clean up on termination.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New tests for abort scenarios.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQRZ5N6005WI43**: [test-failure] test-check-audit-gate.mjs / test-close-work-items.mjs / test-run-release.mjs (6 node failures) — failing test (still open, critical priority)
- **SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB**: Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status — uses trap/finally pattern for exit cleanup (relevant pattern to follow)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Is the abort specifically SIGKILL, or does SIGTERM also fail to restore status?" — Answer (Map): SIGTERM should be handled by Python's finally blocks, but SIGKILL cannot be caught by Python at all. The fix must handle SIGKILL via a wrapper mechanism. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Can a wrapper process approach work here?" — Answer (Map): Yes, a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death is an acceptable approach. Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Audit stuck in in_progress when run-release is aborted
